title: Cramer Remix: 'It's too soon' to buy even this top-notch industrial stock
summary: Jim Cramer advises against buying Emerson Electric despite its quality, citing macroeconomic concerns like trade talks with China and oil prices. He also expressed frustration with hedge funds' influence on market swings based solely on oil prices and called for federal regulators to investigate rapid sell-offs like the one on Christmas Eve. Additionally, Cramer discussed backlash from his suggestion for Apple to acquire Epic Systems and gave his preferred fintech stocks: Mastercard, PayPal, and Visa.

title: The Story Behind the Real (And Fake) Names on Credit Cards
summary: This article delves into the origins of placeholder names seen on credit card marketing materials, revealing whether they belong to real people or fictional identities. It uncovers the stories behind names like CF Frost on American Express cards, D. Barrett on Chase cards, and Chris L Martin on Bank of America promotions. The piece explains why banks use these names to engage potential customers and reflects on the broader practice of displaying a name on a credit card.

title: Introducing Apple Card, a new kind of credit card created by Apple
summary: Apple announced Apple Card, a new credit card designed for iPhone, focusing on simplicity, transparency, and privacy, aiming to help customers achieve a healthier financial life. It integrates into the Apple Wallet app, offers Daily Cash rewards, eliminates fees, and provides real-time spending insights. Apple is partnering with Goldman Sachs and Mastercard for its launch in the US this summer.

title: Bank of America tech chief is skeptical on blockchain even though BofA has the most patents for it
summary: Bank of America's tech and operations chief, Cathy Bessant, expresses skepticism about blockchain's immediate utility, despite the bank holding more blockchain-related patents (82) than any other financial firm. Bessant views blockchain as a technology still searching for a clear use case that scales beyond individual transactions. While the bank is "future-proofing" with patents, Bessant is particularly doubtful about public blockchains and wary of projects like JPM Coin's actual usage volume.

title: Apple Card vs. American Express Platinum: A High-End Credit Card Face-Off
summary: This article compares the new Apple Card with the American Express Platinum, highlighting their features, fees, interest rates, and perks. While Apple aims to disrupt the credit card industry with its fee-free model and integrated ecosystem, American Express Platinum offers a suite of luxury benefits. The comparison aims to help consumers understand where Apple Card fits into the high-end credit card market.

title: Earnings preview: American Express (AXP) to cash in on cardmember spending, partnerships in Q1
summary: American Express (AXP) is expected to report diluted earnings of $1.98 per share on revenues of $10.45 billion for Q1 2019, driven by increased cardmember spending and strategic partnerships. The company has consistently topped earnings expectations, and analysts have a mixed "hold" and "buy" rating on the stock with an average price target of around $118.

title: BMO Bank of Montreal To Implement Mastercard Send In Canada
summary: BMO Bank of Montreal is implementing Mastercard Send in Canada to provide faster, cheaper, and more transparent international payment services for its business and commercial banking clients. This partnership aims to enhance cross-border payments by allowing clients to send money efficiently and securely to bank accounts in over 75 countries, with future plans to expand to mobile wallets and cards. This initiative addresses the increasing demand for cost-effective cross-border solutions for global businesses.

title: SWOT Analysis of American Express - AMEX SWOT Analysis
summary: This article provides a comprehensive SWOT analysis of American Express, detailing its strengths such as strong brand recognition and high market capital, and weaknesses like a declining traveler's cheque business and lack of debit cards. It also identifies opportunities for market expansion and increased product offerings, alongside threats from strong competitors and volatile economic conditions. The analysis highlights AMEX's position as a prestigious financial service provider and outlines potential areas for growth and concern.

title: Adaptive Enterprises Are Growing Three Times Faster Than Their Competitors
summary: Adaptive enterprises, which proactively reconfigure themselves based on insights and leverage technology platforms, are growing 3.2 times faster than industry averages. These firms distinguish themselves by acting on insights, leveraging platforms for new value, and fostering a culture that embraces change, as exemplified by companies like CVS, Mastercard, and Netflix. The article emphasizes that while agility is foundational, true future market leadership requires this advanced level of adaptiveness.

title: VGT ETF Down On Tech Stock Woes
summary: The Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT) experienced a downturn due to woes in the technology stock market, particularly with the Nasdaq being rattled. The article highlights Apple's decline due to regulatory concerns and mentions the broader risk associated with the concentration of VGT's portfolio in a few major tech companies. Analysts from D.A. Davidson noted increasing regulatory disruption potential for tech titans like Amazon, Apple, Facebook, and Google globally.

title: OpenText announces fresh partnerships and talks Google at Enterprise World
summary: OpenText announced expanded partnerships at its Enterprise World event, notably with Google Cloud, where OpenText will be the preferred partner for Enterprise Information Management Services (EIM). The company emphasized alignment with partners and a cloud-first strategy, while also maintaining support for on-premises deployments. OpenText also revealed a new partnership with Mastercard to offer spot financing to automotive clients.

title: Capital One data breach: The main takeaway for consumers
summary: The Capital One data breach, affecting over 106 million customers, highlights the critical need for consumers to actively monitor and protect their financial information. Experts advise regular transaction monitoring, varied passwords, security questions, and suspicious activity alerts to prevent personal financial crises. While consumers have a role, companies are ultimately responsible for data protection and implementing robust cybersecurity measures to prevent such breaches.

title: Here’s how the stocks held by Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway have performed in 2019
summary: This article examines the performance of stocks held by Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway in 2019, highlighting top performers like Mastercard and Costco, and significant underperformers like Kraft Heinz. It delves into the challenges faced by Kraft Heinz, including changing consumer tastes, accounting issues, debt, and an SEC investigation, and mentions Buffett's regrets regarding his investment in the company.

title: Bangkok tops Paris, London as world's most-visited city MasterCard
summary: Bangkok has been named the world's most-visited city for the fourth consecutive year by MasterCard, attracting 22.8 million visitors. Despite this, Thailand's tourism industry faces challenges due to a drop in Chinese arrivals, though this has been partially offset by an increase in Indian tourists. The government is working to boost tourism by extending visa fee waivers and anticipating future growth from emerging markets.

title: Crypto firm hired actors to pose as Comerica, Mastercard execs, bank says
summary: Comerica Bank is accusing crypto firm VRB of brand infringement after VRB allegedly used actors posing as Comerica and Mastercard executives to scam investors. VRB falsely claimed Comerica as a financial backer and guaranteed refunds, while Mastercard also denied any affiliation with the company. This incident highlights the prevalence of scams in the cryptocurrency market.

title: Sallie Mae launches credit cards aimed at student loan borrowers
summary: Student loan lender Sallie Mae has introduced three new cash-back credit cards specifically designed for college students and recent graduates. These cards, Ignite, Accelerate, and Evolve, aim to help borrowers establish credit responsibly and offer incentives such as bonuses on cash-back rewards used to pay down student loans. While the cards have no annual fee and an introductory 0% APR, potential cardholders should be aware of the variable APR ranging from 14.99% to 24.99% after the introductory period.

title: Visa, Mastercard Say They Just Made Mobile Shopping a Lot Easier
summary: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and Discover have partnered to launch a one-click checkout option for online mobile shopping, aiming to simplify the purchasing process and reduce "online cart abandonment." This new service competes with existing offerings from PayPal and Apple Pay by allowing consumers to save their payment details and bypass the need to manually enter credit card information for each transaction. The initiative seeks to address the frustration associated with inputting credit card details on small screens, which currently costs retailers billions in lost sales.

title: Cashless no more: Kroger Visa credit card ban ended following year-long fight over fees
summary: Kroger has ended its more than year-long ban on Visa credit cards, now accepting them at all of its stores nationwide. The supermarket giant had previously stopped accepting Visa at some subsidiaries due to "excessive fees," but has since reversed its decision. While the specific terms of the resolution are unknown, analysts view this as a win for Visa and the broader card industry, avoiding potential consumer-unfriendly surcharges or lost sales for merchants.

title: American Express Relaunched the Green Card—And It's Greener Than the Original
summary: American Express has relaunched its Green Card, now named Green from Amex, featuring a design primarily manufactured from plastic recovered from oceans and coasts in partnership with Parley for the Oceans. This initiative is part of Amex's broader commitment to eliminate single-use plastics and includes a card recycling program and options for customers to redeem reward points for eco-friendly products. Other financial institutions like Mastercard and Visa are also taking steps to reduce their environmental impact, reflecting a growing consumer demand for environmentally conscious companies.

title: Shaking the Latin American Equilibrium: The Petrobras & Odebrecht Corruption Scandals
summary: This article details the massive Petrobras and Odebrecht corruption scandals, which began as a small money laundering investigation in Brazil and uncovered widespread bribery and fraud across Latin America. It examines the profound impact of these scandals, including major settlements with U.S. authorities and the resulting push for political and corporate reform in the region. The author discusses how these events are challenging deeply entrenched institutional corruption, possibly leading to more transparent and competitive markets.

title: Elavon to acquire Sage Pay, a gateway that competes with Stripe, PayPal and Adyen, for $300M
summary: Elavon, a subsidiary of US Bancorp, announced its acquisition of Sage Pay for £232 million ($300 million). This deal aims to boost Elavon's presence in the European e-commerce market, particularly in the UK and Ireland, and reflects the ongoing consolidation trend in the fragmented payment processing industry. Sage Group, Sage Pay's owner, is divesting payment assets to focus on accounting and payroll software.

title: American Express offers merchants up to $450K sign-on bonus to boost acceptance
summary: American Express is offering sign-on bonuses of $10,000 to $450,000 to encourage businesses to accept its payment cards, aiming to close the acceptance gap with Mastercard and Visa. This strategy is part of a multiyear effort to expand its merchant network and counter higher interchange fees, despite AmEx customers typically spending more. The company has focused on strategically targeting holdout merchants and salesforce incentives to achieve this growth.

title: PAGS Stock Price, Quote & Chart | PAGSEGURO DIGITAL LTD-CL A (NYSE:PAGS)
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of PagSeguro Digital Ltd. (NYSE: PAGS) stock, including its current price of $9.37, performance metrics, and key statistics. It also covers technical and fundamental analysis ratings from ChartMill, recent earnings reports, analyst forecasts, and company profile information. Investors can find data on market capitalization, P/E ratio, dividend yield, and future growth expectations for this financial technology company.

title: Visa and MoneyGram Partner on Debit Card Cross Border Transactions
summary: MoneyGram has partnered with Visa to enhance its debit card solution, allowing nearly instant cross-border fund transfers to select countries via Visa Direct. This expansion leverages Visa's real-time push payments platform for international P2P debit card deposit services, starting with the U.S. to Spain and the Philippines. The collaboration aims to capitalize on the growing demand for real-time P2P payments, especially through mobile transactions, and boost MoneyGram's digital business.

title: Vanguard Information Technology ETF: Expensive, But Should Be Okay To Continue To Own
summary: The article analyzes the Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT), noting its portfolio of large-cap technology stocks with competitive positions. Despite its current premium valuation, the fund is deemed suitable for continued ownership due to the long-term growth outlook of its holdings and their "moaty" characteristics like recurring revenues and strong ecosystems.

title: Top 10 Tech Acquisitions of 2019 | YearEnder | Toolbox
summary: The article reviews the top 10 tech acquisitions of 2019, totaling $100 billion, by major tech and financial giants like Apple, Nvidia, Salesforce, FIS Global, Mastercard, and PayPal. These acquisitions aimed to diversify product offerings, introduce new features, and expand market presence in areas such as fintech, security, software, and hardware. The article also discusses key lessons businesses can learn from these acquisition trends, highlighting the drive for digital transformation and customer-centricity.

title: American Express catches up to Visa, Mastercard in acceptance, it reports
summary: American Express announced it has achieved "virtual parity" in merchant acceptance with Visa and Mastercard by adding 1 million U.S. merchants last year. This achievement is attributed to programs like OptBlue, which enticed small businesses with lower costs, and sign-on bonuses. Despite lingering public perception of higher fees, the gap in interchange fees between AmEx and its competitors is narrowing.

title: Swiping their way higher: Visa, Mastercard could be the next $1 trillion companies
summary: Visa and Mastercard are rapidly increasing in market value, with stocks up roughly 50% in the past year, leading some to believe they could be the next $1 trillion companies by 2023. Their growth is driven by the global shift towards cashless financial transactions and online shopping, with both companies holding significant shares of the credit and debit card market. Despite potential risks from increased competition and regulation, both firms are actively seeking acquisitions to boost their financial technology integration.

title: BlackRock is donating $589 million to bolster financial inclusion
summary: BlackRock is donating its remaining stake in PennyMac Financial Services, valued at $589 million, to philanthropic efforts focused on financial inclusion and socio-economic mobility. Half of the shares will go to the existing BlackRock Charitable Fund, and the other half to the newly created BlackRock Foundation, which will invest in assets and make grants to promote savings habits and access to savings funds. This initiative aligns with CEO Larry Fink's focus on companies serving a social purpose and sustainability.

title: Mastercard CEO Ajay Banga to step down, insider Michael Miebach tapped
summary: Mastercard CEO Ajay Banga will step down at the start of 2021 and will be replaced by Chief Product Officer Michael Miebach. Banga, who became CEO in April 2010, will transition to executive chairman, while Miebach will also join the board and assume the role of president on March 1, 2020. This announcement follows a day after Mastercard issued a revised, lower revenue growth forecast for the first quarter due to the viral outbreak in China, causing shares to fall in premarket trading.

title: Technology trumps consumer staples in the hunt for quality
summary: This article argues that the traditional strength of consumer staples has waned, while the technology sector now offers superior investment opportunities, particularly when viewed through a "franchise power/growth framework." It highlights the shift in leadership from consumer staples to IT, attributing technology's rise to strong business franchises, network effects, and a move towards subscription-based software models. The author also compares the portfolio weightings and performance of various quality investment funds, showing a trend towards higher tech exposure.

title: Apple Credit Card: five facts to know ahead of the US August launch
summary: Apple Inc. has partnered with Mastercard Inc. and Goldman Sachs Group Inc. to launch the Apple Card in the U.S. in August, aiming to reimagine the classic credit card with a focus on simplicity, transparency, and privacy. Key features include enhanced financial control, integration with Apple Wallet for spending insights, real-time finance management, and cash-back rewards. The card also boasts advanced cybersecurity solutions and privacy protections, including specific measures to prevent fraudulent activity and ensure user data is not sold to third parties.

title: The true fintech pioneer in the US? American Express is breaking borders
summary: American Express and Nova Credit have partnered to launch a new service in the US fintech landscape. This collaboration enables immigrants and expats from several countries to use their international credit history to obtain US credit cards, addressing a significant barrier for many new residents. This initiative aims to integrate non-native populations into the US financial system by translating international credit records into US-equivalent scores.

title: Western Union makes offer to buy MoneyGram
summary: Western Union Co. is reportedly seeking to acquire rival money transfer company MoneyGram International Inc. A takeover offer has been made, though no final decision has been reached. This potential merger would bring together two major U.S. money transfer service providers in a declining market.

title: Trump Administration Will Not Renew Marriott OFAC License To Manage Hotels In Cuba
summary: The Trump Administration announced its decision not to renew Marriott International's OFAC license to manage hotels in Cuba, specifically the Four Points Sheraton in Havana, forcing Marriott to cease operations by August 31. This move is seen as a continuation of the administration's policy to reverse Obama-era initiatives with Cuba, viewing commercial activities as unduly benefiting the Cuban government. Marriott expressed disappointment but hopes to return if U.S. government policy changes.

title: Fortune 500 Tapestry CEO Jide Zeitlin Quits For Personal Reasons After Less Than A Year On Job
summary: Jide Zeitlin, CEO of Fortune 500 Tapestry Inc., resigned for personal reasons after less than a year, amidst allegations of an inappropriate personal relationship predating his tenure. His departure reduces the number of Black CEOs in Fortune 500 companies to three. Zeitlin had also been a vocal advocate against racism and for Black Lives Matter.

title: In the search for a new king of credit cards, some surprise names emerge
summary: The credit card market is dynamic, with rewards constantly changing, making the search for a "king of credit cards" an ongoing process. Non-bank providers like Rogers World Elite Mastercard and Brim Financial have emerged as strong contenders, offering competitive rewards and no foreign transaction fees, challenging traditional bank offerings. Consumers are advised to look beyond their primary banks and compare features to find cards that best suit their spending habits and reward preferences, as even top-tier cards can be devalued over time.

title: BMO signs deal to offer digital chequing accounts in U.S. through Google Pay
summary: Bank of Montreal (BMO) has partnered with Google to offer digital chequing accounts in the U.S. via Google Pay, joining an initiative launched by Google last November. This collaboration allows BMO to expand its customer reach through Google's platform, offering financial insights and budgeting tools to users, while Google benefits from banks' stability and access to financial data. This move highlights the banking industry's trend of collaborating with tech giants to counter digital disruption and leverage their vast user bases.

title: BBVA te invita al Cosquín Rock Festival Online este fin de semana
summary: BBVA is inviting customers to the Cosquín Rock Festival Online this weekend, which will be a two-day interactive and immersive digital event featuring over 50 artists from across Hispanoamerica. BBVA customers in Argentina can purchase tickets with Visa and Mastercard credit cards in three interest-free installments. The festival promises a unique online experience including chat functions, meet & greets, and VR experiences.

title: American Express Said to Be in Talks to Buy Kabbage for $850 Million
summary: American Express is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire online lender Kabbage for an all-cash deal worth up to $850 million. This potential acquisition would further solidify American Express's presence in the small-business market, a sector from which 30% of its revenue is derived. The move follows similar high-value fintech acquisitions by Mastercard and Visa, indicating a broader trend among traditional card networks to integrate fintech innovation.

title: American Express makes Kabbage acquisition official
summary: American Express has officially acquired Kabbage's team, fintech products, data platform, and intellectual property for small businesses. The deal significantly enhances AmEx's reach into the small business market, which accounts for about 30% of its revenue, and comes after Kabbage played a major role in the Paycheck Protection Program. This acquisition is part of a larger trend of credit-card networks bolstering their technology assets through fintech acquisitions.

title: Jamie Dimon of JP Morgan Chase and other CEOs aim to hire 100,000 New Yorkers by 2030
summary: A group of CEOs, led by Jamie Dimon of JPMorgan Chase and the head of Google, formed the New York Jobs CEO Council with the goal of hiring 100,000 disadvantaged New Yorkers or people of color by 2030. This initiative aims to provide training, apprenticeships, and entry-level positions to address economic inequities exacerbated by the COVID-19 crisis, particularly in communities of color. The program, which includes companies like Goldman Sachs and Amazon, also plans to expand beyond entry-level roles and potentially to other cities.

title: KKR wraps up $739 mn purchase of Korean waste management firms
summary: KKR has finalized its $739 million acquisition of two South Korean waste treatment companies, ESG Co. Ltd. and ESG Cheongwon Co. Ltd., from Anchor Equity Partners. This deal marks KKR’s first buyout in Korea in two years, aligning with its KKR Global Impact Fund's focus on environmental solutions. The ESG Group, which primarily handles medical waste, is expected to benefit from the growing senior-care market and rising treatment prices.

title: Ally partners with Mastercard’s Vyze to enter retail point-of-sale lending
summary: Ally Financial is partnering with Mastercard's Vyze to enter the retail point-of-sale (POS) lending market, offering installment loans ranging from $500 to $40,000 with interest rates between 9.99% and 26.99%. This move follows Ally's earlier acquisition of Health Credit Services and its pivot from a credit card model to focus on POS lending, anticipating significant growth in this sector. The partnership aims to provide merchants with a powerful digital option to offer consumers stable installment loan choices, catering to a market segment that favors fixed monthly payments over traditional credit cards.

title: JetBlue makes credit card deal with Puerto Rican bank Popular
summary: JetBlue has announced a new credit card agreement with Puerto Rican bank Popular. The airline will be launching two new Mastercard options in Puerto Rico: one with no annual fee and another with a $99 annual fee. This deal expands JetBlue's credit card offerings in the region.

title: SoundHound Inc. Partners With Mastercard to Voice-Enable Consumer Shopping Experiences
summary: SoundHound Inc. has partnered with Mastercard to integrate its Houndify voice AI platform into Mastercard's retail solutions, focusing initially on voice-enabled drive-throughs for quick-service restaurants. This collaboration aims to provide low-touch, high-engagement shopping experiences and enhance customer safety and convenience, especially in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. The technology will allow customers to place complex orders naturally, with initial pilots starting at White Castle in October 2020.

title: Mastercard expands AI drive-thru testing to White Castle
summary: Mastercard is expanding its AI-powered drive-thru testing to several White Castle locations and a Dunkin' restaurant, following previous tests to enhance ordering efficiency and customer experience. The platform incorporates vehicle recognition and voice ordering technology from Rekor Systems and SoundHound, aiming to provide personalized menus and reduce labor costs in the QSR space. This move reflects a broader industry trend towards contactless ordering and payment methods, accelerated by the pandemic.

title: Amid Covid’s Impact, Installment Pay Gets a Lift With New Offerings From Mastercard And Sezzle
summary: Mastercard and online installment startup Sezzle are expanding their installment payment offerings, capitalizing on increased consumer demand due to Covid-19's impact. Mastercard is integrating with TSYS and other technology providers to allow cardholders to elect installment payments before, during, or after a purchase. Sezzle is launching a virtual card compatible with Google Pay and Apple Pay, enabling its buy-now-pay-later service for in-store purchases for the first time.

title: Mastercard partners with Global Payments’ TSYS to expand installment offerings
summary: Mastercard has partnered with TSYS, a Global Payments company, to offer consumers more flexible payment options by enabling them to split transactions into installments before, during, or after checkout. This collaboration aims to meet the growing demand for flexible payment solutions amidst economic uncertainties, enhancing Mastercard's buy-now-pay-later ecosystem and benefiting issuers and merchants. The partnership focuses on increasing consumer choice, control, and simplicity at checkout, ultimately aiming to boost consumer acquisition, loyalty, and approval rates while decreasing cart abandonment.

title: The digital transformation: speed and convenience drive B2C payments
summary: Digital transformation is rapidly changing B2C payments, driven by customer demand for speed and convenience, especially among Millennials. The article highlights how technological advancements, particularly mobile technology and payment networks, are enabling businesses to digitize low-value consumer payments like refunds and rebates, significantly reducing costs and enhancing customer satisfaction. This shift leverages network effects, contextual remittance, and enhanced security measures to create a strong value proposition for both payers and customers.

title: Market value of big fintech companies rises to $1 trillion, more than the largest banks
summary: The market capitalization of major fintech companies like Visa, MasterCard, Square, and PayPal has surpassed $1 trillion, exceeding the value of the six largest U.S. banks. This shift reflects investors' favor towards software-based tech companies during the pandemic and fintech's increasing push into traditional banking services. Meanwhile, traditional banks face pressure from low interest rates and potential loan defaults.

title: 10 monopolies and why they make good investments
summary: This article explores the investment potential of monopolies and oligopolies, guided by insights from Peter Thiel and Warren Buffett on competitive advantage. It identifies ten companies with strong monopolistic or oligopolistic market positions, such as Amazon, Google, Facebook, Visa, and Airbus, highlighting their market shares and business models. The author also discusses the transient nature of monopolies, using examples like Kodak and Nokia, and suggests investing in a "moat" ETF for diversified exposure to such companies.

title: PayPal and Mastercard Expand Debit Card Offering to More European Businesses
summary: PayPal and Mastercard are expanding the availability of the PayPal Business Debit Mastercard to five new European countries: Austria, France, Ireland, Italy, and Spain, in addition to existing markets like Germany, the UK, and the US. This debit card provides small businesses with instant access to their PayPal funds, offers unlimited 0.5% cash back on eligible spending, and has no monthly or foreign exchange fees. The expansion aims to support small businesses, particularly during economic challenges, by facilitating easier access to funds and providing rewards.

title: Wells Fargo CEO Scharf comes under fire over diversity comments
summary: Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf faced significant backlash for comments made in June regarding the limited pool of Black talent for senior roles, despite the bank's pledge to double Black leadership and tie diversity efforts to executive compensation. Scharf later apologized, clarifying that his remarks were "insensitive" and stemmed from "unconscious bias." The controversy highlights broader issues of racial diversity in the financial industry, prompting other major banks and financial companies to announce their own diversity initiatives.

title: ACI Worldwide and Mastercard to Collaborate and Advance New Payment Solutions and Experiences for Customers
summary: ACI Worldwide and Mastercard have announced a global partnership to provide real-time payment solutions. Their collaboration will initially focus on offering central infrastructure, payments localization, and access solutions to central banks, scheme operators, and financial institutions worldwide. This partnership aims to accelerate the development and adoption of real-time and multi-channel payment platforms, leveraging the growing market opportunity in account-to-account payments.

title: Home Depot’s loyalty update gets mobile-first treatment
summary: Home Depot has updated its Pro Xtra loyalty program, integrating it with a mobile app to offer home-improvement professionals easier ways to earn and redeem points. The app provides a "mobile-first" experience, allowing users to track purchases and savings via a virtual ID barcode, and includes gamified features to encourage repeat business. This move reflects Home Depot's broader strategy of leveraging technology to enhance customer engagement and capitalize on strong sales growth seen during the pandemic.

title: P&G Shareholders Send Resounding Message Calling for Diversity Disclosure
summary: Procter & Gamble shareholders voted 37% in favor of a resolution from As You Sow, demanding greater disclosure on diversity data related to employee promotion, recruitment, and retention. Investors are concerned P&G's extensive advertising campaigns on race relations may be perceived as exploitative without accompanying internal diversity metrics. This shareholder action highlights a demand for concrete data to demonstrate the effectiveness of P&G's diversity, equity, and inclusion programs, contrasting with other companies that have agreed to increased reporting.

title: Banner Bank Sticks to Its Philosophy of Keeping it Simple with Its Selection of Rewards-Packed Mastercard Offerings
summary: Banner Bank emphasizes simplicity and transparency in its Mastercard credit card offerings, including the TruRewards® Mastercard® and the World Rewards® Mastercard®. These cards offer competitive APRs, no annual fees, and straightforward rewards redemption options like travel, cash back, and gift cards to local businesses. The bank also provides additional benefits like rental collision waivers and a unique fixed-rate balance transfer program, alongside a new mobile app for enhanced card control.

title: PayPal launches crypto payment platform
summary: PayPal is launching a new service allowing U.S. customers to buy, sell, and hold various cryptocurrencies, and eventually use them to pay at 26 million merchants. This move is expected to significantly increase the mainstream acceptance of digital currencies, with PayPal managing price volatility risks for merchants by converting crypto to fiat for transactions. The service will initially include Bitcoin, Ethereum, Bitcoin Cash, and Litecoin, and will expand to Venmo and international markets.

title: The Truth About Prepaid Cards
summary: This article examines prepaid cards, distinguishing common misconceptions from their actual utility. It explains that while these cards do not build credit, they can be a financially sensible option for managing expenses or providing temporary financial stability, especially for the underbanked. The piece emphasizes evaluating costs, understanding fine print, and considering prepaid cards as part of a broader financial strategy.

title: Why Regulators Are Saying ‘Yes’ to Mastercard-Finicity But ‘No’ to Visa-Plaid
summary: Regulators have approved Mastercard's $825 million acquisition of data-networking company Finicity, while simultaneously suing to block Visa's $5.3 billion bid for its rival, Plaid. The disparity in regulatory action stems from the Department of Justice's concern that Visa's acquisition of Plaid would eliminate a potential competitor in the debit-networking sphere, thereby strengthening what it perceives as Visa's monopolistic position in that market. Conversely, the DoJ views Mastercard's acquisition as less likely to create such an anti-competitive environment, given Mastercard's different market position.

title: HDFC bank services restored after hours of an outage affecting UPI and card payments
summary: HDFC Bank's services, including UPI, card payments, and ATM transactions, were restored on Sunday after an outage that began Saturday evening. Customers had reported issues with online banking, credit/debit cards, and linked third-party services. The bank acknowledged the outage was due to a data center issue and apologized for the inconvenience, though intermittent problems may still occur as systems stabilize.

title: Behind BNY Mellon’s war against B2B checks
summary: BNY Mellon is leading an effort to modernize B2B payments, moving away from labor-intensive and fraud-prone paper checks towards efficient digital solutions. They are utilizing tools like Bottomline Technologies' Paymode-X, The Clearing House’s Real-Time Payments (RTP) network, and Zelle to offer faster, more secure transactions with integrated data exchange. The bank's initiatives aim to mirror the ease of consumer payment experiences while providing the robust security and documentation features required by businesses, positioning them as an innovator in the rapidly evolving financial landscape.

title: Building Black Friday e-commerce experiences with JAMstack and Cloudflare Workers
summary: This article discusses how Cloudflare Workers can be used to build scalable e-commerce experiences, particularly for high-traffic events like Black Friday. It highlights a sample open-source e-commerce app built on Workers, integrating with Stripe for payments and Sanity.io as a headless CMS. The post details the implementation of the frontend using Nuxt.js and Workers Sites, and the backend handling of checkout sessions, webhooks, payment distribution, and email delivery, all within the Workers environment.

title: Equifax Announces New President of Canadian Business
summary: Equifax has appointed Sue Hutchison as the new Canada Region President, effective November 30. John Hartman, President of Equifax International, highlighted her strong expertise in lending, digital payments, and financial services as crucial for accelerating growth. Hutchison previously held senior leadership roles at Mastercard, Payments Canada, D+H Corporate, HSBC, and Bank of America, bringing extensive industry experience to Equifax.

title: Digital Currencies (XBT, EXT, XRP) Are Set to Go Mainstream Says PayPal CEO
summary: PayPal CEO Dan Schulman believes digital currencies are poised to go mainstream as more merchants adopt a "digital first" approach to payments. He noted that the shift towards smartphone payments, QR codes, and digital wallets creates a natural environment for digital currencies to flourish. This outlook was shared at the Web Summit conference, emphasizing the growing integration of digital payment solutions.

title: Fidelity National Information Services Inc. stock rises Friday, outperforms market
summary: Shares of Fidelity National Information Services Inc. (FIS) rose 1.75% on Friday, closing at $149.86 and outperforming both the S&P 500 Index and the Dow Jones Industrial Average. This increase ended a two-day losing streak for the company's stock. Despite the rise, the stock remained $8.35 below its 52-week high.

title: Capital One Halts Buy-Now-Pay-Later Credit Card Transactions
summary: Capital One has become the first major card company to prohibit customers from using its credit cards for buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) transactions, citing potential risks for both customers and banks. This decision comes despite a surge in the BNPL market, with companies like Afterpay experiencing significant growth and PayPal launching its own installment payment product. Afterpay acknowledges the impact on a small percentage of its customer base, while Capital One clarifies that debit card and checking account BNPL purchases remain unaffected.

title: Deal of the Year: American Express buys Kabbage
summary: American Express acquired Kabbage's team, fintech products, data platform, and internet protocol for small businesses in a deal estimated between $750 million and $1 billion. This acquisition highlights both companies' strategies to expand beyond their traditional services, with Kabbage moving beyond lending into checking accounts and AmEx aiming to strengthen its small-business offerings and become more essential to its customers. The move by American Express follows similar acquisitions by Visa and Mastercard, demonstrating a broader trend in the payments industry to integrate data aggregation and expand services.

title: Tipalti extends credit card capability through new partnership
summary: Tipalti has partnered with Plastiq to allow businesses to pay invoices using corporate credit cards, even if suppliers don't accept them directly. This collaboration aims to provide businesses with increased access to capital, card rewards, and improved short-term cash flow, automating accounts payable processes. While offering flexibility, the solution involves a fee from Plastiq, and companies must carefully weigh the benefits against potential costs and risks.

title: Paul Harris QC leads for claimants as £14bn Mastercard consumer claim to proceed after historic Supreme Court ruling
summary: The UK Supreme Court has upheld a decision allowing a £14 billion consumer claim against Mastercard to proceed, overturning a previous Competition Appeal Tribunal (CAT) judgment. This ruling paves the way for 46 million UK consumers to seek compensation for losses incurred due to Mastercard's illegal actions. Paul Harris QC is leading the claimant's case, marking a significant development in UK consumer protection law.

title: Mastercard Incorporated v Merricks
summary: The Supreme Court ruled in favor of Mr. Merricks against Mastercard in a significant competition collective action case. This groundbreaking decision, affecting 46.2 million consumers and billions in losses, clarified the criteria for collective proceedings, removing stringent evidential thresholds at the certification stage and allowing for aggregate damages. Tristan Jones, who acted for the intervener Which?, has provided further analysis on the decision's implications.

title: Mastercard Faces $18.6B Class Action in UK
summary: Mastercard faces a massive 14 billion-pound ($18.6 billion) class action lawsuit in the UK after losing a Supreme Court battle over illegal swipe fees. The decision permits a claim representing 46 million consumers and facilitates future mass claims by making it easier to bring such cases. Mastercard maintains the case is flawed and driven by "hit and hope" lawyers.

title: PayPal Announces Additional $5 Million Grant Program for Black-Owned Businesses as COVID-19 Crisis Continues
summary: PayPal Holdings, Inc. announced an additional $5 million grant program for Black-owned businesses in the U.S., extending its previous $10 million program. This initiative is part of PayPal's broader $530 million commitment to support Black-owned businesses, strengthen minority communities, and fight economic inequality, especially critical as the COVID-19 crisis continues to disproportionately impact these businesses. The grants aim to help businesses stabilize, reopen, and grow, complemented by capacity-building programming in partnership with organizations like AEO, Deloitte, and Facebook.

title: Why Wall Street Would Love to See a Merger of FIS and Global Payments
summary: Although merger talks between Global Payments (GPN) and Fidelity National Information Services (FIS) have reportedly ended, analysts remain bullish on both stocks, viewing the discussions as a positive indicator for valuations and future industry consolidation. Wall Street believes a merger would create significant synergies and cost savings, boosting FIS's revenue and earnings per share. The payment processing industry has seen considerable consolidation recently, and a combination of FIS and Global Payments would strengthen their market position.

title: JPMorgan is acquiring a major credit card rewards business in a bet that travel will rebound next year
summary: JPMorgan Chase is acquiring cxLoyalty Group's credit card rewards business, including its technology platforms and travel agency, in anticipation of a significant rebound in pleasure travel post-pandemic. The acquisition will integrate cxLoyalty's operations into JPMorgan's retail division, aiming to enhance experiences for Chase customers and gain better control over its rewards program. This move is expected to give JPMorgan unique deals with hotel and airline partners through its dual user and supplier platform.

title: JPMorgan Chase to acquire key business of Stamford-based cxLoyalty
summary: JPMorgan Chase is acquiring the global loyalty division of Stamford-based cxLoyalty Group Holdings, a major provider of credit card loyalty and engagement programs. This deal includes cxLoyalty's technology platforms, travel agency, and gift card businesses, with about half of cxLoyalty's 3,100 employees moving to JPMorgan Chase. The acquisition reflects JPMorgan Chase's confidence in the future of travel and its commitment to enhancing travel benefits for its Chase customers.

title: Alibaba,Tencent shares fall after reports of US investment ban
summary: Shares of Chinese tech giants Alibaba and Tencent dropped following reports that the Trump administration was considering banning U.S. investments in the companies. This potential move is seen as a significant escalation in U.S.-China tensions. The ban could impact capital markets, given the combined $1.3 trillion market value of Alibaba and Tencent.

title: Mastercard And Partners Will Test Common Android Phones And Tablets As Contactless POS Devices
summary: Mastercard is launching "Tap on Phone," a service that allows common Android smartphones and tablets to accept contactless payments without additional hardware. This initiative, developed by Mastercard Labs, aims to leverage the increasing adoption of contactless payments by consumers and merchants. Mastercard has partnered with NMI, Global Payments Inc., and CEG for distribution and initial testing, while adhering to PCI Security Standards.

title: Value vs. Growth: Widest Performance Gap on Record
summary: In 2020, large-growth funds significantly outperformed large-value funds, with an average return of 34.8% compared to value's performance. This 32 percentage point gap marked the widest performance difference on record, surpassing even the dot-com bubble year of 1999. The consistent underperformance of value strategies, especially amplified in 2020, has led to a substantial widening of longer-term return gaps across various market capitalizations.

title: Walgreens Expands Financial Services Business Strategy, in Partnership with Synchrony and Mastercard
summary: Walgreens is expanding its financial services offerings by partnering with Synchrony and Mastercard to launch co-branded credit and prepaid debit cards. These cards will integrate with the myWalgreens loyalty program, offering cash rewards and additional benefits. The initiative aims to create new revenue streams and enhance customer loyalty and personalization in health and well-being.

title: Walgreens Inks Credit-Card Deal with Synchrony, Mastercard
summary: Walgreens will launch new credit cards and a prepaid debit card in partnership with Synchrony Financial and Mastercard. The initiative, announced in a statement, aims to introduce financial services options for the drugstore chain's customers. This move signals Walgreens' entry into the credit card market.

title: GM, Goldman Sachs, Mastercard join forces on credit card venture
summary: General Motors, Goldman Sachs, and Mastercard are collaborating to introduce co-branded, rewards-based credit cards in 2021. Goldman Sachs will serve as the issuing bank for GM's credit card programs starting in September, with Mastercard continuing as the network provider. This follows Goldman's acquisition of GM's credit card business for approximately $2.5 billion, aiming to enhance the credit card experience for GM customers.

title: Goldman Sachs to issue credit cards for General Motors
summary: Goldman Sachs announced it will become the issuing bank for General Motors' credit card business starting September 2021, part of its strategy to expand its consumer banking division. This move follows previous media reports of Goldman Sachs winning the bid over Barclays in a $2.5 billion deal. Mastercard will remain the network for the card, and this marks Goldman's second significant credit card partnership after its collaboration with Apple in 2019.

title: Goldman Sachs to Take Over General Motors’ Credit-Card Business
summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. has signed an agreement to take over General Motors Co.'s credit-card portfolio, becoming the issuer for the automaker's credit-card programs. The targeted start date for this new partnership is September, with Mastercard Inc. continuing as the network for the cards. The terms of the deal were not disclosed by either company.

title: MA - Mastercard Incorporated - Ordinary Shares - Class A Quote, Price, Charts & News
summary: This article provides real-time stock information for Mastercard Incorporated (MA), including its current quote, price changes, and market data. It displays key market indices like SPX, Dow 30, QQQ, and VIX, along with Mastercard's specific stock performance for the day.

title: Walgreens partners with Synchrony and Mastercard
summary: Walgreens is expanding its financial services by partnering with Synchrony and Mastercard to launch new credit and prepaid debit cards. These cards will integrate with the myWalgreens loyalty program, offering cardholders cash rewards and other benefits. The co-branded credit card will provide accelerated rewards for purchases, particularly in the health and wellness category.

title: New Sam's Club Mastercard Rewards Program By Synchrony Unlocks Additional Value On Sam's Club Purchases
summary: Sam's Club, Synchrony, and Mastercard announced a new Sam's Club Mastercard rewards program offering enhanced value for cardholders, particularly Sam's Club Plus members. Plus members can now earn up to a total of 5% back on eligible Sam's Club purchases by combining rewards from the Mastercard and their Plus membership. The program also includes benefits like 5% cash back on fuel, 3% on dining, digital rewards, and contact-free payment options.

title: NatWest Group switches all debit cards to Mastercard
summary: NatWest Group has moved all of its retail and business debit cards, totaling 16 million cards across NatWest, RBS, Ulster Bank, and Coutts brands, from Visa to Mastercard. This strategic shift follows similar moves by other major banks and aims to provide more tailored payment options and enhanced digital experiences for cardholders. Mastercard anticipates that this will expand its debit card presence to one in three consumer debit cards in the UK and one in four in Ireland.

title: Sam’s Club teams up with Synchrony, Mastercard for rewards program
summary: Sam's Club has partnered with Synchrony and Mastercard to launch an enhanced Sam's Club Mastercard rewards program, offering members more digital features and incentives. The program, announced on January 27, includes 5% cash back on eligible purchases for Sam's Club Plus members and features contactless payments, online rewards access, and mobile app integration. This initiative aims to help customers save money and earn rewards, especially in light of the past year's financial challenges.

title: HBC partners with Neo Financial to launch new Hudson’s Bay MasterCard
summary: Hudson's Bay Company (HBC) has partnered with Neo Financial to introduce a new Hudson's Bay MasterCard, following the end of its relationship with Capital One. This move is part of HBC's "digital-first strategy" to enhance customer experience through digital applications, cash back, and rewards. The partnership aims to combine technology and retail innovation, offering a more advanced and rewarding financial product to nearly two million existing Hudson's Bay credit card holders.

title: Bitcoin hits record highs as more companies embrace crypto boom
summary: Bitcoin reached new record highs following announcements from Mastercard Inc. and Bank of New York Mellon Corp. about their increased embrace of cryptocurrencies. This surge is further fueled by Tesla CEO Elon Musk's significant investment in Bitcoin and his public support for cryptocurrencies, attracting more traditional financial institutions to the digital asset class. Despite the growing adoption, critics continue to warn of speculative bubbles and potential misuse.

title: Mastercard and Jennifer Hudson Launch Multi-Faceted Platform Supporting Black Women-Owned Businesses
summary: Mastercard has launched the Strivers Initiative, a new platform designed to support Black women-owned businesses, which have been significantly impacted by the pandemic. The initiative, featuring GRAMMY Award-winner Jennifer Hudson, includes a grant program in partnership with Fearless Fund, an educational road show, and an advertising campaign to elevate the visibility of these entrepreneurs. This effort builds on Mastercard's half-billion-dollar commitment to support Black communities and aims to provide financial tools, capital, and digital resources to help these businesses thrive.

title: Melvin Capital raised put option on GameStop Class A shares to 6 mln in Q4 2020
summary: Melvin Capital Management increased its put option on GameStop Class A shares to 6 million in Q4 2020 from 5.4 million, according to a disclosure, though this doesn't reflect January's liquidation of its GameStop position. The hedge fund also reported new positions and increased stakes in other companies like Airbnb, Facebook, Mastercard, Visa, Hilton Worldwide Holdings, and Nike. These details come from regulatory 13F filings, which provide insight into institutional investors' quarterly holdings.

title: La primera tarjeta de crédito en España cumple medio siglo
summary: BBVA, originally Banco de Bilbao, introduced the first credit card in Spain in 1971, revolutionizing payment methods by offering an alternative to physical cash. Fifty years later, BBVA continues to innovate with its cards made from recycled materials and its Aqua card, which features enhanced security through the absence of embossed numbers and a dynamic CVV. The article highlights the evolution of these cards from basic plastic to sophisticated digital payment options, emphasizing increased security measures and sustainability efforts.

title: Discover and Sezzle Partner On Buy Now-Pay Later
summary: Discover and Sezzle have announced a partnership that will integrate Sezzle's buy now, pay later (BNPL) options into the Discover Global Network, allowing select U.S. merchants to offer interest-free installment payments. This collaboration aims to accelerate Sezzle's business development and provide Discover's merchants with more payment flexibility as the BNPL market continues its significant growth. The article highlights the increasing popularity of BNPL for consumers and the card networks' interest in this expanding payment method, especially for higher ticket items.

title: Banco Santander lanza Getnet, una nueva red de pagos en Chile
summary: Banco Santander has officially launched Getnet, its new payment network in Chile, after several months of testing with over 250 businesses. This initiative aims to increase competition in the Chilean payments market by offering faster payment processing (same-day or multiple times daily), compatibility with various card types, and competitive commission rates. Getnet provides different plans for businesses and aims to be an innovative and secure solution for transactions.

title: American Express Co. stock falls Tuesday, underperforms market
summary: American Express Co. (AXP) stock fell 3.44% on Tuesday, closing at $145.10, despite an overall positive trading session for the broader market. This drop ended a six-day winning streak and left the stock $6.36 short of its 52-week high reached the previous day. The company's performance lagged behind competitors like Visa Inc. and Mastercard Inc.

title: Emerald Card clients have received their third stimulus
summary: H&R Block announced that third stimulus payments to Emerald Cards finished processing on March 16, 2021, ahead of the IRS's anticipated March 17th arrival for the first wave of payments. The company partnered with the IRS to ensure a smoother process for its clients receiving these crucial payments. Clients can check their payment status via the myBlock mobile app, Emerald Card support line, or the IRS Get My Payment site.

title: End of an Era: L Brands Founder Leslie H. Wexner Permanently Leaving Victoria’s Secret
summary: Leslie H. Wexner, the founder of L Brands and Victoria's Secret, along with his wife Abigail, will not seek reelection to the company board, marking the end of an era for the retail giant. Their departure comes as L Brands plans to separate into two businesses, with Wexner citing the company's strong position and new board appointments. The decision follows previous leadership changes and scrutiny over Wexner's past associations and Victoria's Secret's declining sales and inability to adapt to changing market conditions.

title: Les Wexner steps away from board of Victoria’s Secret owner L Brands
summary: Les Wexner, the 83-year-old founder of L Brands, announced his and his wife Abigail's decision not to seek re-election to the company's board, effectively cutting ties with his decades-old retail empire. This move comes as L Brands prepares to separate its Victoria's Secret and Bath & Body Works businesses and follows previous controversies surrounding Wexner's association with Jeffrey Epstein. Two independent female directors will replace them on the board.

title: Les Wexner exits board, severs last ties to retail empire
summary: Les Wexner, the billionaire founder of L Brands, is severing his last ties with the retail empire by not seeking re-election to the company's board of directors. This decision follows his earlier step down as CEO and chairman and comes as L Brands plans to separate its Victoria's Secret and Bath & Body Works businesses. Wexner's reputation was also affected by his association with the late Jeffrey Epstein.

title: Life Well Rewarded: Barclays Launches New Credit Cards for AARP Members
summary: Barclays US Consumer Bank has launched a new suite of co-branded credit cards for AARP members, including the AARP Essential Rewards Mastercard and the AARP Travel Rewards Mastercard. These cards offer valuable rewards such as cash back on medical expenses, drug store purchases, gas, restaurants, travel, and more, with no annual fee. Barclays has also committed to supporting the AARP Foundation's Essential Connections program, aiming to combat social isolation among older adults through donations tied to new accounts and eligible purchases.

title: KKR, Sequoia, others invest in small business lender Five Star
summary: Five Star Business Finance Ltd, a lender to small businesses, has raised $234 million (Rs 1,700 crore) from new and existing investors, valuing the company at $1.4 billion (Rs 10,300 crore). The funding round included investments from KKR's Global Impact Fund and TVS Capital as new investors, alongside increased participation from existing investors Sequoia Capital India and Norwest Venture Partners. The capital will be used to expand Five Star's lending business, which focuses on providing financial services to small and micro enterprises, and in making small housing loans to middle and lower-income segments.

title: Mastercard battles to limit scope of $19 billion UK class action
summary: Mastercard is fighting to reduce the scope of a £14 billion ($19.3 billion) class action lawsuit in the UK, specifically opposing the inclusion of 14 million deceased individuals in the claim. The case, led by former financial ombudsman Walter Merricks, alleges Mastercard overcharged consumers with excessive interchange fees between 1992 and 2008. Mastercard disputes the claim, arguing that the attempt to include deceased persons is a "nullity" and that new members are time-barred, while also resisting the addition of compound interest.

title: Women in Business: Nmachi Jidenma
summary: Nmachi Jidenma, Head of Scouts & Partnerships at Sequoia Capital, is highlighted for her significant contributions to venture capital and business development. Her career includes leading global strategy at WhatsApp, driving strategic partnerships at Facebook, and spearheading global business development at PayPal. Jidenma is also actively involved in philanthropic work and serves on several boards, demonstrating her influence across various sectors.

title: Walgreens launches a bank acount
summary: Walgreens is launching its own mobile and online bank account in partnership with InComm Payments and MetaBank, with availability expected in the second half of 2021. The account includes a Mastercard debit card and mobile spend tracking, building on Walgreens' existing loyalty programs. This initiative aims to expand financial services for customers and create new revenue streams for the company.

title: Mastercard to invest $100 mln in Airtel Africa's mobile money unit
summary: Mastercard will invest $100 million in Airtel Africa's mobile money operations, valuing the business at $2.65 billion. This investment aligns with Airtel Africa's strategy to monetize its mobile money unit by selling up to a 25% stake, following a previous $200 million investment by TPG's The Rise Fund. The mobile money unit, operating under the Airtel Money brand, offers various financial services across 14 African countries.

title: Mastercard Announces New Partnerships with DoorDash and HelloFresh, While Expanding Those with Fandango, Lyft, and ShopRunner to Enhance Offerings for Cardholders
summary: Mastercard has announced new partnerships with DoorDash and HelloFresh and expanded existing collaborations with Fandango, Lyft, and ShopRunner. These initiatives aim to enhance value for World and World Elite consumer credit cardholders by offering rewards, discounts, and benefits for online purchases, reflecting the significant growth in digital spending. The new offerings, starting April 1st, include free DashPass trials, discounts on DoorDash and HelloFresh orders, Lyft credits, Fandango rewards, and free ShopRunner membership.

title: 71.7% of All Payments in India to be Digital by 2025
summary: A report by ACI Worldwide and GlobalData predicts that 71.7% of all payments in India will be digital by 2025, driven by a significant increase in real-time and electronic transactions. India led globally in real-time payment transactions in 2020 with 25.5 billion, and the pandemic has accelerated the adoption of digital payments worldwide. Mobile wallet usage also reached a historic high in 2020.

title: OppFi Teams Up with Mastercard, First Electronic Bank and Deserve to Introduce OppFi Card
summary: OppFi announced a partnership with Mastercard, First Electronic Bank, and Deserve to launch OppFi Card, a new mobile-first credit card. This initiative aims to expand credit access for millions of consumers underserved by traditional financial products. The OppFi Card, issued by First Electronic Bank, will allow instant digital access for cardholders and is expected to launch in the second half of 2021.

title: Swvl’s co-founder and former CTO Ahmed Sabbah launches Telda, a Venmo-like app for Gen Z in Egypt
summary: Ahmed Sabbah, co-founder and former CTO of Swvl, has launched Telda, a fintech app aimed at Gen Z in Egypt, similar to Venmo. Telda offers digital accounts with a free Mastercard-powered card for online and in-store payments, cash withdrawals, and facilitates easy money transfers between users. The app has partnered with a local bank to operate in Egypt and plans to expand to Saudi Arabia soon.

title: With the Deadline Having Passed, Less Than Half of Sellers Comply With Gas Pump EMV
summary: Less than half of fuel and convenience store sellers have complied with the EMV mandate for gas pumps, despite the April 17th deadline, according to a survey by ACI Worldwide Inc. This means liability for fraud at non-compliant pumps now shifts to the merchants. Issues such as a shortage of technicians and the COVID-19 pandemic have been cited as reasons for the delayed compliance, with many sellers still uncertain when they will achieve full EMV readiness.

title: Mastercard snaps up identity verification company Ekata for $850M
summary: Mastercard has acquired Ekata Inc., an identity verification company, for $850 million. Ekata provides global identity verification data through APIs and SaaS to help businesses assess digital risk and comply with regulatory requirements like Know Your Customer. This acquisition aims to bolster Mastercard's fraud prevention and digital identity programs, enabling safer online interactions for its corporate clients.

title: India c.bank bans AmEx, Diners Club from issuing new cards for violating data rules
summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has banned American Express and Diners Club International from issuing new cards to domestic customers starting May 1 due to violations of local data storage rules. Both companies had failed to comply with the directive requiring Indian payments data to be stored locally for supervisory access. American Express and Discover Financial Services, owner of Diners Club, expressed disappointment but are working with the RBI to resolve the concerns.

title: India restricts American Express from adding new customers for violating data storage rules
summary: India's central bank, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), has barred American Express and Diners Club from onboarding new customers starting May 1 due to violations of local data-storage regulations. These rules, introduced in 2018, mandate payments firms to store all Indian transaction data within the country. While existing customers remain unaffected, American Express expressed disappointment but is working with the RBI to resolve the issue.

title: 52% of gas station merchants fall short of new chip card standard
summary: Only about 48% of major U.S. gas station merchants were expected to meet the April 17 deadline for installing EMV chip card readers, leaving over half vulnerable to fraud costs. These merchants will now bear the expense of counterfeit fraud at pumps not equipped with the new chip technology, while those compliant will have fraud losses covered by card issuers. The delay in adoption is attributed to challenges like technician and parts availability, overseas manufacturing, and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Mastercard partners with Gemini exchange to launch cryptocurrency rewards credit card
summary: Mastercard Inc. and U.S. cryptocurrency exchange Gemini are launching the first credit card that offers digital currency rewards on purchases. Users can earn up to 3 percent back in bitcoin or other cryptocurrencies, which will be deposited into their Gemini account. This move reflects deepening involvement of major payment firms in the emerging asset class.

title: FIS links with NYDIG to offer Bitcoin services
summary: FIS, a major U.S. payments processor, is partnering with NYDIG to allow its bank clients to offer Bitcoin services, including buying, selling, and holding the cryptocurrency. This move responds to growing customer demand and aims to help banks attract and retain customers while providing fee income. FIS is also acquiring a stake in NYDIG, a company specializing in Bitcoin technology and financial services.

title: Visa vs. Mastercard — should you buy either stock now?
summary: This article questions whether investors should buy Visa or Mastercard stock despite their high valuations due to their expected brisk earnings growth. Both companies are highlighted as mature and stable within the highly profitable payment processing industry, which avoids the credit risk and capital requirements of traditional lenders.

title: Amex pushing beyond cards to woo small businesses
summary: American Express is expanding its services beyond traditional payment cards to better serve small and midsize businesses, a crucial segment accounting for a significant portion of its loan mix and card member receivables. The company is offering a range of supplier payment and cash-flow management solutions, including its One AP automation platform and Kabbage for lending and working capital, aiming to deepen relationships with existing clients and attract new ones. This move reflects a broader industry trend towards B2B solutions, with Amex leveraging its closed-loop system and bank charter to differentiate itself from competitors like Visa and Mastercard.

title: Under the hood of Australia’s largest sustainable ETF
summary: This article examines the BetaShares Global Sustainability Leaders ETF (ASX:ETHI), Australia's largest sustainable fund, highlighting its strong performance and strict exclusion criteria while also noting the inclusion of companies accused of tax evasion. It delves into the fund's methodology, its holdings (dominated by tech and financial services), and its performance compared to other funds, discussing the complexities of defining "sustainable" in investing. The piece also raises concerns about animal testing and tax minimization among some of ETHI's holdings.

title: Moneygram to Rollout “Buy & Sell BTC in Cash” Across its US Locations
summary: MoneyGram International, a money transfer company, has partnered with Coinme Inc., a licensed digital currency exchange, to allow customers to buy and sell Bitcoin (BTC) for cash across its U.S. locations. This collaboration aims to provide a more accessible way for millions to engage with cryptocurrency, especially first-time buyers who may be intimidated by online exchanges. The service will bridge cryptocurrency with local fiat currency through MoneyGram's extensive retail network, with plans for international expansion.

title: Payments giant FIS makes another crypto move, expanding in Europe
summary: Payments giant FIS is expanding its crypto services in Europe through a new partnership with UK-based cryptocurrency exchange CEX.IO. FIS will provide card management and processing for CEX.IO's new line of crypto-based debit cards. This move follows FIS's earlier announcement to enable its bank clients to offer Bitcoin services, highlighting the increasing mainstream adoption of cryptocurrencies among major financial players.

title: PR News | Prosek, ICR Deliver Flywire’s Timely IPO - Wed., May 26, 2021
summary: Prosek Partners and ICR Inc. are handling public relations and investor relations for Flywire, a global payments company that successfully raised $250 million in its initial public offering (IPO). Flywire plans to use these funds for technology development, solutions, and potential acquisitions. The IPO's timing is strategic, coinciding with an anticipated surge in post-pandemic travel, for which consumers are seeking seamless payment options.

title: Parthenon Capital, Tiger Global fuel payments sector ‘boom’
summary: The payments sector is experiencing a significant boom, driven by increased investment from private equity, venture capital, and hedge funds, as well as accelerated digital adoption due to COVID-19. This has led to rising fundraising amounts and valuations for payment technology companies. Firms like Parthenon Capital and FTV Capital, who have long specialized in payments, are now facing heightened competition from major investors like Tiger Global, pushing up prices and making deal-making more challenging.

title: 10 Largest Class Action Settlements in American History
summary: This article lists and describes the ten largest class action settlements in American history, detailing the circumstances and monetary values of each. These settlements range from issues like defective breast implants and accounting fraud to major events like the Volkswagen emissions scandal and the BP Gulf of Mexico oil spill, with the largest being the 1998 Big Tobacco settlement. The piece highlights how these lawsuits have impacted consumers and speculates on future large settlements, particularly in technology and privacy.

title: Mastercard's 'True Name' Feature Expands Across the Globe this Pride Month
summary: Mastercard is expanding its "True Name" card feature globally this Pride Month, allowing transgender and non-binary individuals to use their preferred names on their credit and debit cards. This expansion is facilitated by Global Payments for its TSYS issuer customers, with bunq and Monzo launching in Europe, and BM Technologies and Republic Bank & Trust Company expanding deployment in North America. The initiative aims to enhance inclusivity and prevent negative experiences for cardholders whose IDs do not match their presentation.

title: Mastercard, Ambev back away from Copa America as players vent COVID-19 concerns
summary: Major sponsors Mastercard and Ambev have withdrawn their support for the Copa America tournament, which was unexpectedly relocated to Brazil despite a severe COVID-19 outbreak. This decision comes as players and public health experts express concerns over hosting the event amidst a raging pandemic. The Brazilian soccer team also cited humanitarian concerns but committed to participating in the tournament.

title: BofA’s Pay to Card Brings the Bank Into the Fast-Developing Market for Speedy Payouts
summary: Bank of America has launched Pay to Card, a new service allowing fast payouts to consumers globally, responding to increased demand from the gig economy and e-commerce growth. The service processes payments within five minutes domestically and often within half an hour internationally, leveraging debit card details for consistency across borders. Analysts see BofA having an advantage due to its existing business clients and consumers compared to fintechs that have developed similar payout platforms.

title: Switzerland's PostFinance Selects FICO Falcon Platform to Protect Nearly 3 Million Debit Cards with AI
summary: FICO announced that Switzerland's PostFinance will use the FICO Falcon Platform to protect nearly 3 million debit cards with AI-powered payments card protection. The platform will manage suspicious behavior and scams, which have been increasing during the pandemic. PostFinance aims to provide the strongest possible fraud protection for its customers while ensuring frictionless transactions.

title: Visa pilots US merchant phone-tap system
summary: Visa has launched a tap-to-phone payment pilot program for U.S. merchants, allowing them to accept contactless payments via their Android smartphones without additional hardware. The initiative, initially rolling out in Washington D.C. and then five other major cities, aims to support small and medium-sized businesses in adapting to increased digital payment preferences post-pandemic. This technology has been available in 30 other countries since last year and helps reduce friction, limit touch, and lessen reliance on cash transactions.

title: Suit Claims Visa, MasterCard Are Fixing Prices On Square Fees
summary: Visa and MasterCard are facing a new class-action lawsuit from small business owners. The lawsuit alleges that the credit card companies conspired with banks to illegally increase transaction fees on purchases made via Square devices, violating antitrust laws in 26 states. The complaint was filed on June 16, 2021, in the US District Court for the Eastern District of New York.

title: Oficial en Argentina: los bancos comunican que Visa no brinda más el seguro de alquiler de autos
summary: Banks in Argentina, specifically BBVA, have officially announced that Visa will discontinue its car rental insurance benefit starting July 1, 2021. This change affects rentals commencing on or after that date, regardless of when they were paid. The article advises travelers to review insurance coverage carefully to avoid surprises, especially since Mastercard's car rental insurance (which requires declining the Collision Damage Waiver) is still available.

title: Payment solutions: Transaction evolution and the IoT
summary: The article explores the rapid evolution of payment solutions, driven by increased connectivity, fintech, and the Internet of Things (IoT). It highlights how the COVID-19 pandemic significantly accelerated the shift towards digital and contactless payments, with QR codes and online transactions seeing massive uptake. Experts discuss the move towards a cashless society, the growing importance of personalized customer experiences through data and AI, and the impact of Open Banking in streamlining financial transactions.

title: SZA NFTs center of new American Express crypto rewards
summary: American Express has entered the NFT market by selling non-fungible tokens featuring R&B singer SZA, whose virtual concert the company recently hosted. The initial sale of 10 NFTs to concert attendees for $100 quickly sold out, demonstrating card member interest in the NFT space. This move, along with similar initiatives from MasterCard and Visa, highlights credit card companies' efforts to embrace blockchain innovation amid concerns that the technology could disrupt their traditional business models.

title: Push-to-Card Payments Push Financial Services Forward
summary: The article discusses the accelerated adoption of push-to-card payments as an efficient alternative to traditional payment methods like checks, particularly within business operations. It highlights a partnership between Avidia Bank and KyckGlobal, where KyckGlobal's platform enables businesses to disburse funds instantly to individuals via debit cards, expanding push payments beyond peer-to-peer transactions. The piece emphasizes the importance for financial institutions to embrace cutting-edge technology and integrate such solutions to remain competitive in the evolving digital payments landscape.

title: Visa rolls out BNPL for merchants
summary: Visa is expanding its Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) services to merchants in Canada, partnering with Global Payments to allow eligible cardholders to use installment payment options at the point of sale. This move capitalizes on the growing BNPL market, with Visa planning to offer the service through credit union Desjardins and Scotiabank next month. The service, called Visa Installments, aims to increase purchase totals and conversion rates for merchants while providing consumers with flexible payment options without new loan applications.

title: Discover invests $30 million in BNPL company Sezzle
summary: Discover Financial Services is investing $30 million in the buy now-pay later (BNPL) provider Sezzle to integrate a BNPL solution on Discover's card network. This investment follows an earlier agreement to enable U.S. merchants to process BNPL payments on the Discover Global Network, positioning Discover to compete with rivals like Mastercard and Visa in the growing BNPL market. Discover will also collaborate with Sezzle on a referral program to introduce its credit and debit products to Sezzle’s customer base.

title: Mastercard Creates Simplified Payments Card Offering for Cryptocurrency Companies
summary: Mastercard is enhancing its card program for cryptocurrency companies to simplify the conversion of cryptocurrency to traditional fiat currency. This initiative aims to reduce friction and offer greater consumer choice by enabling crypto companies to provide card programs for spending digital assets. Mastercard is collaborating with key partners like Paxos, Circle, Evolve Bank & Trust, and Metropolitan Commercial Bank to facilitate this new capability.

title: Card companies go green, but hurdles remain
summary: The payment card industry faces environmental challenges due to plastic card waste and transaction processing emissions. Companies are exploring solutions like recycling cards, using alternative materials such as ocean-recovered plastic or metal, and promoting digital-first cards, driven by increasing consumer demand for eco-friendly options. Despite these efforts, hurdles like recycling complexities, higher costs for sustainable materials, and consumer reluctance to fully abandon physical cards remain.

title: Kredivo, the Leading Digital Consumer Credit Platform in Southeast Asia, Announces Plans to Become a Publicly Traded Company via Merger with VPC Impact Acquisition Holdings II
