Capital One may argue the merger increases competition against dominant players like Mastercard and Visa, potentially lowering consumer costs.

title: Capital One-Discover merger raises concerns about effects on credit card holders
summary: The proposed $35 billion merger between Capital One and Discover is facing significant scrutiny from lawmakers and regulators due to concerns about reduced competition and potential negative impacts on credit card holders, including higher interest rates. This deal comes at a time of heightened oversight following recent bank failures and a report suggesting consumers could save money with smaller banks. Experts anticipate a drawn-out regulatory process given the current antitrust stance.

title: How Capital One’s $35 Billion Discover Merger Could Affect Consumers
summary: Capital One's proposed $35 billion acquisition of Discover Financial Services would create the largest credit card issuer in the US by loan volume, aiming to compete with Visa and Mastercard. While critics express concerns about the deal's size, some analysts believe it could lead to a more robust challenger in the payment network landscape, potentially benefiting consumers through increased competition. The merger represents the largest announced globally this year.

title: ¿Quién es el dueño de BBVA en México?
summary: BBVA México, una de las instituciones financieras más grandes del país, tiene sus raíces en la fusión de varios bancos, incluidos los españoles Bilbao y Vizcaya, y posteriormente Argentaria y Bancomer. Aunque cuenta con un CEO y presidente, la propiedad del banco se encuentra distribuida entre cinco grandes empresas a nivel mundial. Estas compañías poseen porcentajes significativos de las acciones de BBVA.

title: Capital One’s Discover Acquisition Would Reshape US Credit Card Industry
summary: Capital One plans to acquire Discover Financial Services in an all-stock transaction valued at $35.3 billion, a move that would significantly reshape the US credit card industry. The deal faces intense scrutiny from antitrust authorities and politicians concerned about market consolidation. If approved, the merger would create a credit card giant, with Capital One shareholders owning 60% of the combined entity.

title: Capital One-Discover: A Competition Policy and Regulatory Deep Dive
summary: This report provides a detailed competition policy and regulatory analysis of Capital One's proposed $35.3 billion acquisition of Discover. The analysis concludes that the deal is likely to face significant regulatory hurdles due to concerns about increased interchange revenue, Capital One's access to a de facto government backstop, and the fortification of its market power in the credit card industry. The article delves into potential antitrust law violations, financial stability risks, and public interest concerns that could derail the merger.

title: Worldpay Global Payments Report 2024: Digital Wallet Maturity Ushers in a Golden Age of Payments
summary: The Worldpay Global Payments Report 2024 highlights the rapid growth and maturity of digital wallets, projecting their global transaction value to exceed $25 trillion by 2027. This growth is driven by consumer preference, ease of use, and enhanced security, making digital wallets a dominant payment method both online and at point-of-sale. The report also notes the impact of government investment in real-time payment infrastructures, particularly in regions like Brazil and India, and emphasizes the importance of collaboration across the payments ecosystem to further innovation.

title: American Express sued in merchants' class-action over 'swipe' fees
summary: American Express is facing a proposed class-action lawsuit from thousands of U.S. merchants alleging overcharging for credit and debit card "swipe" fees. The lawsuit, filed in Rhode Island federal court, claims American Express uses "non-discrimination provisions" to prevent merchants from encouraging customers to use payment methods with lower transaction fees, violating antitrust law. This legal action mirrors previous "swipe-fee" allegations against Visa and Mastercard, with merchants seeking to block American Express policies and recover lost funds.

title: Visa And Mastercard Agree to Merchant Rate Cuts and Acceptance Changes in a Major Settlement
summary: Visa and Mastercard have reached a landmark settlement with merchants regarding interchange rates and acceptance rules, potentially saving merchants nearly $30 billion. The agreement involves capping and rolling back credit card processing fees and simplifying rules for surcharging and card acceptance. This settlement aims to resolve long-standing lawsuits and must be approved by a U.S. District Court.

title: Capital One pledges to give Discover’s network a boost
summary: Capital One is arguing to federal regulators that its acquisition of Discover would increase competition in the card network market, which is currently dominated by Visa and Mastercard. Capital One plans to invest significantly in Discover's network to boost its scale, brand awareness, and merchant acceptance, as well as improve its technology and risk management. This move is intended to challenge the market dominance of Visa, Mastercard, and American Express, despite potential antitrust concerns and calls from lawmakers to block the deal.

title: Mastercard, Visa reach $30 billion settlement over credit card fees
summary: Visa and Mastercard have agreed to an estimated $30 billion settlement to reduce credit and debit card fees for merchants, which could lead to lower prices for consumers. This antitrust settlement, one of the largest in U.S. history, resolves litigation dating back to 2005. The agreement includes a reduction in interchange rates for three years and a cap for five years, along with the removal of "anti-steering" provisions.

title: Visa, Mastercard reach $30 billion settlement over credit card fees
summary: Visa and Mastercard have reached an estimated $30 billion settlement to limit credit and debit card fees for merchants, one of the largest antitrust settlements in U.S. history. The agreement, which requires court approval, aims to resolve most claims in nationwide litigation that began in 2005. While proponents say it offers substantial savings for merchants that could be passed on to consumers, some critics argue the relief is temporary and insufficient to address high swipe fees.

title: Visa, Mastercard to cut interbank card fees as part of agreement
summary: Visa Inc. and Mastercard Inc. have reached an agreement with the U.S. merchant community to lower interchange fees on credit cards, settling nearly two decades of litigation. This agreement, which requires court approval, will reduce fees for merchants for five years, aiming to save small businesses an estimated $30 billion. It also offers merchants more flexibility in payment acceptance and provides funding for training programs.

title: Emirates NBD, Marriott Bonvoy® and Mastercard Unveil Two New Co-brand Credit Cards in the United Arab Emirates
summary: Emirates NBD, Marriott Bonvoy, and Mastercard have launched two new co-branded credit cards in the UAE, expanding on an existing partnership. These cards, available in World Elite and World tiers, offer exclusive travel benefits, Marriott Bonvoy Elite status, and the ability to earn points on everyday purchases, targeting different consumer segments. Limited-time offers for new cardholders include up to 200,000 bonus points or two Free Night Awards.

title: What’s in Cap One’s Wallet?
summary: Capital One's blockbuster bid for Discover, valued at $35.3 billion, positions it to compete with major credit/debit card issuers and networks like Visa, Mastercard, and AmEx. The acquisition offers competitive advantages such as increased economies of scale through Discover's network and Pulse, potential downward pressure on merchant fees, and a path for Capital One to expand its global card business and prepaid card offerings. While regulatory approval is a key question mark, the deal could significantly impact the payments industry for years to come.

title: How Amex is entangled in the Visa-Mastercard settlement
summary: A recent settlement between Visa and Mastercard allows merchants to surcharge credit card transactions, regardless of American Express's policies, aiming to increase competition. This move puts pressure on American Express to either relax its own no-surcharging rules or face potential merchant lawsuits or decreased acceptance. The settlement is predicted to foster competition and could lead to further litigation if Amex maintains its strict policies.

title: Mastercard Announces New Cardholder Benefits to Enhance Health & Wellness, Travel and Lifestyle Rewards for Consumers, Small Businesses
summary: Mastercard has introduced new credit card benefits for consumers and small businesses, partnering with leading brands in health & wellness, travel, and lifestyle sectors. These partnerships, including with Alo Moves, Booking.com, HealthLock, Instacart Business, Lyft, MoviePass, and ResortPass, aim to provide cardholders with enhanced value and savings on everyday essentials and enriching experiences. The benefits address consumer demand for meaningful rewards, offering discounts on accommodations, wellness platforms, medical claim monitoring, ride-sharing, movie subscriptions, and grocery delivery, thereby strengthening cardholder loyalty and financial flexibility.

title: J.P. Morgan Chase, Amazon, Wells Fargo among LinkedIn’s Top Companies of 2024
summary: J.P. Morgan Chase & Co., Amazon, Wells Fargo, Deloitte, and PwC lead LinkedIn's 8th annual Top Companies list for 2024, highlighting 50 best large workplaces in the U.S. The list is compiled using LinkedIn data to measure career success based on promotion rates and skill development. This year's honorees are recognized for their investment in employee experience, including upskilling initiatives and flexible working arrangements.

title: D-Wave Quantum Computer: Commercial QC Pioneer [2024]
summary: This article chronicles the history and technological advancements of D-Wave Systems, recognized as the world’s first commercial quantum computer startup. It details D-Wave's quantum annealing approach, the evolution of its quantum machines from D-Wave One to Advantage2, and its cloud services. The article also addresses the ongoing debate regarding whether D-Wave's annealing machines are truly quantum computers.

title: Supreme Court won’t review Visa, Mastercard ATM fee class certification appeal
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has declined to hear an appeal of class certification in an ATM fees antitrust case against Visa and Mastercard. The lawsuit, filed over a decade ago, alleges that major banks overcharged for access fees at ATM terminals, with the Supreme Court's decision allowing the class action to proceed. The case involves millions of consumers and thousands of ATM operators who claim anticompetitive practices led to inflated ATM surcharges.

title: Fiserv, Inc. (NYSE:FI) Q1 2024 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: Fiserv, Inc. reported strong Q1 2024 results with adjusted earnings per share up 19% and revenue growth of 7%, leading them to raise their full-year EPS outlook. The company's Merchant Solutions segment saw 36% organic revenue growth, driven by Clover's performance and international expansion, while the Financial Solutions segment grew 5% organically, highlighted by Finxact wins and strong digital payment demand. Fiserv emphasized its strategic integration between segments, ongoing capital allocation, and commitment to corporate social responsibility, marking its 40th year in business with sustained growth and innovation.

title: DOJ examines Capital One-Discover deal’s competitive angle
summary: The Justice Department is examining the competitive aspects of Capital One's proposed acquisition of Discover, advising bank regulators who extended their public comment periods on the deal until May 31. Despite concerns raised by critics, Capital One CEO Richard Fairbank maintains the $35.3 billion all-stock transaction will increase payment network competition and benefit consumers, anticipating a close by late 2024 or early 2025. This scrutiny is part of a broader trend of increased antitrust enforcement from the Biden administration and bank regulators.

title: MASTERCARD FOUNDATION INTRODUCES MFAM, A NEW SEPARATE ASSET MANAGEMENT COMPANY, TO SUPPORT ITS PHILANTHROPIC MISSION
summary: The Mastercard Foundation has launched Mastercard Foundation Asset Management (MFAM) Corporation, a new, separate entity designed to manage its growing investment portfolio. MFAM's primary goal is to generate long-term returns that will fund the Foundation's philanthropic mission, which focuses on advancing education and financial inclusion for young people in Africa and Indigenous youth in Canada. John Barker, with over 30 years of experience, has been appointed as MFAM's Chief Investment Officer to lead this initiative.

title: Mastercard Foundation launches Toronto-based asset manager to oversee $47-billion in investments
summary: The Mastercard Foundation has established a new Toronto-based asset management firm, Mastercard Foundation Asset Management (MFAM), to oversee its US$47-billion portfolio. This move aims to modernize its investment strategy by diversifying holdings beyond its original Mastercard stock, gradually selling down 90% of those shares over seven years. Led by CIO John Barker, MFAM will build a diversified portfolio and initially rely on third-party fund managers, with plans for direct investments over time, marking one of the largest greenfield investment startups globally.

title: Merchants urged to file claims for $5.5B payment card settlement
summary: Merchants have until May 31 to file claims for a share of a $5.5 billion settlement stemming from an antitrust case against Visa and Mastercard. The settlement addresses alleged overcharging of interchange fees between 2004 and 2019. Lawyers and the settlement administrator are conducting outreach to ensure eligible businesses, both large and small, are aware of the easy claims process and to combat scams.

title: Citi Enhances the Citi Premier Card with New Benefits to Make Travel Adventures More Rewarding
summary: Citi has rebranded and enhanced its Citi Premier Card, now called the Citi Strata Premier℠ Card, maintaining its $95 annual fee while introducing new benefits. The updated card offers increased ThankYou® Points on travel bookings and EV charging, along with new travel protection benefits and existing perks like a $100 annual hotel benefit. For a limited time, new applicants can earn 75,000 bonus ThankYou Points after meeting spending requirements.

title: 3 Funds With Double-Digit Stakes in a Single Stock
summary: This article examines three equity funds––Fidelity Growth Company (FDGRX), American Century Ultra (TWCUX), and Akre Focus (AKREX)––that hold unusually high, double-digit stakes in single stocks, highlighting the risks associated with such concentrated portfolios. While some funds like Fidelity Growth Company have performed exceptionally due to these bold allocations to companies like Nvidia and Apple, others like Akre Focus demonstrate unique, sometimes unusual, concentrations in stocks like Mastercard and Constellation Software. The author notes that such high concentrations, once rare, are becoming more common, but pose meaningful risk for investors.

title: Walmart and Capital One break up
summary: Walmart and Capital One have announced the termination of their credit card partnership, following a federal judge's ruling that Walmart could end the agreement due to Capital One's repeated customer service failures. Existing cardholders can continue to use their Capital One Walmart Rewards cards, with Capital One retaining ownership of the $8.5 billion card loan portfolio. This breakup occurs as Capital One pursues an acquisition of Discover Financial Services, which would make it the largest credit card issuer in the U.S.

title: Visa, Mastercard to pay $197 million to settle consumer ATM fee lawsuit
summary: Visa and Mastercard have agreed to a $197 million settlement in a class-action lawsuit filed by millions of consumers. The lawsuit accused the financial payment companies of colluding to keep ATM cash access fees artificially high. The settlement, which resolves claims from consumers who used bank-operated ATMs since 2007, is subject to court approval.

title: Breakingviews - Capital One scales banking’s Mount Improbable
summary: Capital One's $35 billion bid for Discover aims to create the largest U.S. credit card issuer and a major payments network, but faces significant regulatory and competitive hurdles. CEO Richard Fairbank must convince regulators, merchants, and investors of the deal's value, as integrating Discover's payments network and achieving global acceptance will be a monumental task. The article highlights the low perceived value by investors and the challenges of international expansion in retail banking.

title: Coming of Age for Millennials: American Express Nails It Again
summary: American Express is successfully appealing to younger generations, specifically Gen Z and millennials, by offering premium credit cards with high annual fees that provide significant value to users. This strategic shift has led to substantial financial growth for the company, with stock prices rising and a projected 10%-plus annual revenue growth, and it is largely driven by their ability to book younger cardholders directly into their premium offerings. The company's focus on rewards, service, and cachet continues to foster strong customer loyalty across generations.

title: eBay to Discontinue Acceptance of American Express Payments Starting August 17, 2024
summary: eBay announced its decision to discontinue the acceptance of American Express payments globally starting August 17, 2024. This change is attributed to the "unacceptably high fees" charged by American Express, with eBay calling for more robust regulations to increase competition in the credit card network market. Customers will be notified to transition to alternative payment options available on the marketplace.

title: Wells Fargo Introduces the New Attune℠ World Elite Mastercard®
summary: Wells Fargo and Mastercard have launched the new Attune℠ World Elite Mastercard®, offering unlimited 4% cash rewards on purchases related to fitness, wellness, select sports, recreation, entertainment, and sustainable activities like public transit and thrift stores. Cardholders can earn a $100 cash rewards welcome bonus, and for a limited time, Wells Fargo will donate $50 to Capital Link for each qualifying cardholder. The card also features no annual fee and various security and travel benefits.

title: Amex dismisses impact of eBay’s rejection
summary: EBay announced it will no longer accept American Express payments due to "unacceptably high fees," effective August 17th. American Express, however, downplayed the impact, stating that eBay accounts for less than 0.2% of its total network volume, but criticized eBay for limiting customer payment choices. The move highlights the ongoing tension between merchants and card networks over transaction fees.

title: eBay to End American Express Payments Over Interchange Fees
summary: eBay has announced it will no longer accept American Express card payments due to "unacceptably high" interchange fees, citing the availability of numerous alternative payment methods for its customers. This decision, while potentially saving eBay money in the short term, has been criticized by analysts like Brian Riley of Javelin Strategy & Research, who believes it could harm eBay in the long run by alienating high-spending Amex customers. American Express expressed disappointment, stating that eBay's move is inconsistent with increasing competition at the point of sale and that eBay accounts for a very small portion of their total network volume.

title: Amtrak Launches Limited Time 30,000 Bonus Points Offer for New Amtrak Guest Rewards Preferred Cardholders
summary: Amtrak has announced a limited-time offer for new Amtrak Guest Rewards Preferred Mastercard holders, providing 30,000 bonus points and 5,000 Tier Qualifying Points. This offer, available from June 12 to July 24, 2024, increases the standard bonus by 50% and helps cardholders achieve higher tier status faster. Additional benefits include companion coupons, upgrades, lounge passes, and point rebates on Amtrak travel.

title: Exclusive | Wells Fargo Bet on a Flashy Rent Credit Card. It Is Costing the Bank Dearly.
summary: Wells Fargo is reportedly losing significant money, up to $10 million monthly, on its co-branded credit card with the fintech startup Bilt Technologies. The card, which allows users to pay rent without fees and earn rewards, attracted over a million users but is underperforming due to inaccurate revenue projections. As a result, Wells Fargo is renegotiating its deal with Bilt and scaling back its co-branded credit card initiatives.

title: Advanced Authentication Market size is set to grow by USD 55.87 billion from 2024-2028, increasing volume of online transactions boost the market, Technavio
summary: The global advanced authentication market is projected to grow by USD 55.87 billion from 2024-2028, driven by the increasing volume of online transactions and the adoption of out-of-band (OOB) authentication, according to Technavio. Despite the challenge of rising OTP token costs, the market is set to accelerate at a CAGR of 19.31%, with North America contributing significantly. The growth is fueled by the need for robust security amidst rising cyber threats and the transition from traditional passwords to multi-factor and biometric authentication solutions.

title: Walter Hugh Merricks CBE v Mastercard Incorporated and Others
summary: The Competition Appeal Tribunal has upheld Mastercard's limitation defenses in a major class action, ruling that claims related to infringements before June 20, 1997, are time-barred under English law. The Tribunal found no deliberate concealment or breach of duty by Mastercard and determined that the EU principle of effectiveness does not override English limitation rules in this context. Tim Otty KC represented Mastercard in the case.

title: Visa, Mastercard $30 billion swipe fee settlement rejected by US judge
summary: A U.S. judge rejected a $30 billion antitrust settlement involving Visa and Mastercard over swipe fees charged to merchants. The proposed settlement, intended to resolve long-standing litigation, was opposed by many merchants and trade groups who argued it offered insufficient and temporary relief. This decision could force the card networks to renegotiate or proceed to trial.

title: Amex banks on spending at high-end restaurants
summary: American Express is significantly investing in the high-end restaurant sector through its planned acquisition of Tock, a reservation platform, and Rooam, a payments platform. This strategy aims to capitalize on increased consumer spending in restaurants and offer premium experiences to its cardholders. Analysts view this move as a way to bolster Amex's position in a growing industry and expand their merchant acceptance.

title: NEA: Income Boosts Keep Boosting The Market Price (NYSE:NEA)
summary: The Nuveen AMT-Free Quality Municipal Income Fund (NEA) has seen another income boost as the muni yield curve is upward sloping, offering an advantage over treasury bonds. The fund also has a notable discount to its Net Asset Value (NAV), which could attract value-oriented investors. The author, an investor focused on long-term quality and diversification, holds a long position in NEA.

title: Visa-Mastercard settlement failed to treat merchants ‘equitably’
summary: A proposed settlement between Visa, Mastercard, and merchants was rejected by a judge because it failed to treat large and small merchants equitably. The judge, Margo Brodie, determined that larger merchants, who often negotiate lower interchange rates, would not benefit as much as smaller merchants from the proposed rate reductions and surcharging rights. Additionally, the settlement did not address the "honor all cards" rule, which some larger merchants argue contributes to anti-competitive practices.

title: Legal Fee Tracker: Lawyers' $170 million payday in limbo in credit card swipe fee case
summary: A $170 million legal fee for lawyers who negotiated an antitrust settlement with Visa and Mastercard is now uncertain after a federal judge rejected the proposed deal. The judge found the settlement, intended to limit credit card swipe fees, did not go far enough to benefit merchants despite the substantial legal fees approved. This rejection means attorneys will need to seek further concessions from Visa and Mastercard, likely prolonging the litigation.

title: Visa-Mastercard settlement generates thousands of claim conflicts
summary: A federal judge has granted a 90-day extension, until August 30, for U.S. merchants to file claims in the $5.5 billion Visa-Mastercard class-action settlement. This extension was sought due to tens of thousands of conflicting claims filed for the same businesses, often by multiple third-party filers, and to allow more businesses to submit claims for excessive interchange fees paid between 2004 and 2019. Despite a separate, recent settlement being denied preliminary approval, the current claims process remains unaffected, aiming to ensure as many eligible merchants as possible receive their entitled monetary relief.

title: Oxy, Microsoft clinch “record” carbon removal deal to handle AI-associated emissions
summary: Occidental Petroleum Corp. and Microsoft Corp. have finalized a record carbon removal deal, with Microsoft agreeing to purchase 500,000 metric tons of carbon credits from Occidental's Stratos plant. This agreement helps Microsoft address its growing emissions, particularly those associated with AI, and bolsters Occidental's direct air capture (DAC) technology efforts. Despite high costs and scalability challenges, the deal represents a significant investment in carbon removal, with Occidental planning to expand its DAC plant fleet.

title: Judge rejects proposed $30B Visa, Mastercard settlement over merchant fees
summary: A New York judge has rejected a proposed $30 billion settlement between Visa and Mastercard and a class of merchants regarding credit card swipe fees. The settlement aimed to provide equitable relief by slashing merchant fees, but the rejection was supported by The Retail Industry Leaders Association, which deemed the credit card payment market to be broken. The original settlement, reached after seven years of litigation, included rule changes for merchant fees, estimated to be worth nearly $30 billion, and a $15 million education fund for merchants.

title: Visa announces $2.7 billion preferred stock conversion
summary: Visa Inc. announced the conversion of approximately $2.7 billion in Series B and Series C Convertible Participating Preferred Stock into common stock, following a mandatory assessment related to its 2016 acquisition of Visa Europe. This conversion will result in the issuance of about 99,264 shares of Series A Convertible Participating Preferred Stock, effective July 19, 2024, which will automatically convert into Class A Common Stock upon sale. The move stems from a review of potential litigation liabilities concerning interchange fees in the Visa Europe territory.

title: Mastercard Chair Merit Janow, Molina Healthcare’s Dale Wolf, Board Advisor Ram Charan and CBM Co-founder TK Kerstetter Honored With 2024 Board Leadership Awards
summary: Merit Janow, Dale Wolf, Ram Charan, and TK Kerstetter have been honored with the 2024 Board Leadership Awards by Corporate Board Member. Janow was named "Independent Director of the Year" for her leadership at Mastercard, Wolf received the "Courage in the Boardroom" honor for revitalizing Molina Healthcare, and Charan was recognized for his "Greatest Impact on Corporate Boards." TK Kerstetter will receive a Lifetime Achievement award for his contributions to corporate governance.

title: How Goldman Sachs is building relationships with young talent through its summer internship program
summary: Goldman Sachs is enhancing its summer internship program to attract young talent by offering skill-building opportunities and addressing the expectations of the younger generation. The program focuses on comprehensive recruiting, training, and talent development, seeking to convert interns into professional roles. Omer Tanvir, global head of campus and diversity recruiting at Goldman Sachs, also noted the firm's strategic, three-pillar approach to integrating AI.

title: Travelers Stock Was Down 8% In A Day. Why?
summary: Travelers' stock (TRV) dropped 8% on July 19th after its second-quarter revenues and premiums missed street estimates despite year-on-year growth. The company is currently trading at a 9% discount to its fair value of $224, according to Trefis estimates. Despite underperforming the S&P 500 in 2021 and 2023, Travelers saw a 12% year-over-year revenue increase in Q2 2024, driven by growth in premiums and net investment income, with projections for continued revenue growth in FY2024.

title: Capital One customers sue to block $35 billion Discover merger
summary: Two Capital One customers have filed a class-action lawsuit to block the proposed $35 billion merger between Capital One and Discover Financial, claiming it would reduce competition and drive up prices. The lawsuit, filed in Virginia federal court, argues the deal violates U.S. antitrust law and would diminish competitive forces in the credit card market. Capital One has stated the lawsuit "has no merit," while U.S. regulators have not yet taken formal action on the merger.

title: FTC probes 8 companies for surveillance pricing practices
summary: The FTC has launched a study into "surveillance pricing" practices, ordering eight companies, including Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase, to provide information on how they use consumer data to set prices. The agency is investigating how targeted pricing products, which use personal data like location and past purchases, affect prices for individual consumers. While no wrongdoing is alleged, FTC Chair Lina Khan expressed concerns about potential privacy risks and exploitation of personal information to charge higher prices.

title: Visa Hit By Japan's First-Ever Antitrust Action Against Credit Card Industry
summary: Japan's Fair Trade Commission (FTC) has taken its first-ever antitrust action against the credit card industry, targeting Visa Worldwide Pte Ltd., a subsidiary of Visa Inc. The action addresses alleged monopolistic practices where Visa reportedly forced credit card companies to use its proprietary credit authorization system. Visa has agreed to a voluntary corrective action plan to address these concerns.

title: Visa CEO ‘strongly’ disagrees with class settlement ruling
summary: Visa's CEO, Ryan McInerney, expressed strong disappointment with a federal judge's rejection of a class-action settlement with merchants, calling it unfair despite arguments from merchant lawyers regarding significant savings. He stated that Visa is pursuing a revised settlement, but acknowledges the case could proceed to trial, suggesting a settlement is possible at any stage of the legal process. McInerney also highlighted the complexity of the payments ecosystem, which he believes the judge's decision failed to fully consider.

title: Milberg roils Visa-Mastercard settlement claims process
summary: The law firm Milberg Coleman Bryson Phillips Grossman submitted over 115 fraudulent documents claiming to represent businesses in a $5.5 billion Visa and Mastercard class-action settlement. Milberg blamed a "problematic third-party referral source" for the fake filings involving "high-profile corporations" and has since terminated the relationship, disciplined an employee, and agreed to pay $25,000 to the settlement administrator for costs incurred. The firm also agreed to refer the responsible third party to law enforcement.

title: Why the Capital One-Discover Merger Makes Sense
summary: The proposed $35 billion Capital One-Discover merger is analyzed for its competitive implications in consumer banking, credit card issuance, and payment networks. The article argues the merger makes sense as it will not create a "too big to fail" institution in banking, nor significantly increase credit card market concentration, but rather disrupt the payment network duopoly of Visa and Mastercard by boosting Discover's network volume.

title: Intercontinental Exchange Stock Gained 22% YTD, What’s Next?
summary: Intercontinental Exchange (NYSE: ICE) stock has gained 22% YTD, outperforming the S&P 500, but is still trading 6% below its estimated fair value of $166. The company recently surpassed Q2 FY2024 street estimates with significant revenue growth in its exchanges and mortgage technology segments, despite increased operating expenses impacting net income. Analysts project ICE's total revenues to reach $11.49 billion in FY2024, leading to a GAAP EPS of $6.04 and a valuation of $166.

title: Visa & Mastercard's Singapore sling & an effective income tax rate of 1.1%
summary: The Commerce Commission is reviewing the high fees charged by Visa and Mastercard in New Zealand, which amount to about $1 billion annually for businesses. These global payment giants operate their New Zealand functions through regional hubs in Singapore, allowing them to report substantial profits there while benefiting from significantly lower effective income tax rates (Mastercard at 1.1%, Visa receiving a credit). The article highlights concerns that New Zealanders are paying too much for card payments and that these companies are not contributing significantly to New Zealand's tax revenue despite their lucrative operations in the country.

title: Visa-Mastercard settlement claims deadline postponed
summary: A federal judge has extended the deadline for U.S. merchants to file claims in the $5.5 billion Visa-Mastercard class-action settlement to February 4, 2025. This extension, the second granted this year, aims to ensure more eligible businesses can claim their share, especially after additional data from Visa identified a significant number of class members who did not initially receive claim forms. The settlement resolves a long-running antitrust case concerning excessive interchange fees charged by Visa and Mastercard between January 1, 2004, and January 25, 2019.

title: Capital One slams 'speculative' consumer lawsuit over $35 bln Discover deal
summary: Capital One and Discover Financial Services are seeking to dismiss a consumer lawsuit challenging their proposed $35 billion merger, arguing that the claims of reduced competition and increased prices are speculative. The companies stated in a court filing that the allegations are "too contingent on unknown future events" while U.S. antitrust and regulatory bodies are still reviewing the deal. A U.S. District Judge has scheduled a hearing for October 16th to consider the motion.

title: Alibaba and Mastercard Team Up To Offer New Perks for US Business Owners
summary: Alibaba.com has partnered with Mastercard and Cardless to introduce the Alibaba.com Business Edge Credit Card, offering benefits to US small business owners for cross-border and domestic sourcing. Cardholders can earn 3% cashback or enjoy 60-day interest-free terms on purchases up to $40,000 on Alibaba.com, with additional cashback on other business expenses and all other Mastercard purchases. This initiative aims to support small businesses and contribute to Alibaba's ongoing growth efforts to recover from recent challenges.

title: $197.5M ATM fees class action settlement
summary: Visa and Mastercard have agreed to a $197.5 million settlement regarding a class action lawsuit claiming they charged unlawful surcharges on ATM transactions. The settlement benefits individuals and entities who paid unreimbursed ATM access fees to JP Morgan, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, or banks within the Visa/Mastercard ATM networks between October 1, 2007, and July 26, 2024. Class members can file a claim by January 22, 2025, to receive a cash payment based on the surcharges paid.

title: Americans to get piece of $197.5 million Visa & Mastercard settlement if they paid ATM fee - you just have to apply
summary: Visa and Mastercard have agreed to a $197.5 million settlement following allegations of unlawful surcharges on ATM transactions. Current and former cardholders who paid unreimbursed ATM access fees between October 1, 2007, and July 26, 2024, to specific banks are eligible to claim a portion of the settlement. Individuals who have not been reimbursed or submitted previous claims have until January 22, 2025, to submit a valid claim form online or via mail.

title: $197.5 Million Settlement in ATM Surcharges Class Action
summary: Visa and Mastercard have agreed to a $197.5 million class action settlement for allegedly inflating ATM surcharges through anti-competitive practices. Consumers who paid unreimbursed ATM access fees at U.S. bank ATMs between October 1, 2007, and July 26, 2024, may be eligible to claim a pro rata share of the settlement fund. The deadline to file a claim is January 22, 2025, with final approval granted on June 23, 2025.

title: Salesforce buys Israeli startup Zoomin to feed more data to its AI agents
summary: Salesforce Inc. has acquired Israeli startup Zoomin Software Ltd. for approximately $450 million to enhance its AI agents with unstructured data processing capabilities. Zoomin's technology will be integrated into Salesforce's Agentforce platform, allowing AI agents to deliver more accurate and autonomous responses by leveraging organizational data. This acquisition aims to differentiate Salesforce's AI offerings from competitors like Microsoft by improving the accuracy and utility of its AI agents.

title: PayPal’s stock is having its best year since 2020, and this is a big reason why
summary: PayPal's stock is experiencing its best year since 2020, attributed to product innovations and strategic partnerships under CEO Alex Chriss. After three challenging years, PayPal Holdings Inc. shares are now in positive territory for 2024, signaling a fresh start that has resonated with Wall Street. This turnaround comes after investors questioned the company's future a year ago, following its struggle to regain its pandemic-era glory.

title: Visa Adds $1.5 Billion to Litigation Escrow Account
summary: Visa has authorized a $1.5 billion deposit into its litigation escrow account, established under its U.S. retrospective responsibility plan. This action follows an antitrust lawsuit filed by the U.S. Department of Justice, accusing Visa of stifling competition in the debit card market. Visa's General Counsel Julie Rottenberg called the lawsuit "meritless" and the company plans to vigorously defend itself.

title: CNO Financial Group Appoints Jess Turner to its Board of Directors
summary: CNO Financial Group has appointed Jess Turner, Executive Vice President and Global Head of Open Banking and API at Mastercard, to its board of directors, increasing the board to nine members. Turner brings extensive fintech, financial services, and management experience, which will be instrumental in advancing CNO's strategic growth priorities. Her expertise includes tech-enabled customer experiences, digital product development, and technology security.

title: Visa hit with merchant class action after US Justice Dept antitrust lawsuit
summary: Visa is facing a new class action lawsuit from U.S. merchants, specifically All Wrapped Up Signs and Graphix, following a major antitrust lawsuit filed by the U.S. Justice Department. The merchants accuse Visa (V.N) of anticompetitive practices, including paying rivals not to develop competing networks and threatening merchants with higher fees for using other transaction processing platforms. The lawsuit alleges Visa unfairly dominates the debit card market and seeks to represent potentially hundreds of thousands of businesses harmed by these practices.

title: Visa monopolizes debit card networks, DOJ lawsuit claims
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) has filed an antitrust lawsuit against Visa Inc., alleging the company maintains an unlawful monopoly on debit card networks. The lawsuit claims Visa engages in anticompetitive practices, such as penalizing banks and merchants using alternative payment systems and making agreements with technology companies like Apple, PayPal, and Square to prevent them from becoming competitors. These actions have allowed Visa to control over 60% of debit card transactions and charge more than $7 billion in processing fees, which the DOJ argues are passed on to consumers.

title: Visa and Mastercard: Top Payment Stocks to Watch After Rate Cuts
summary: This article discusses the investment prospects of Visa (NYSE: V) and Mastercard (NYSE: MA) after the Federal Reserve's recent rate cut. While the rate cut's impact on variable-rate credit cards may be minimal, the consistently high APR margins are beneficial for payment processing companies. The article examines each company's growth potential, noting Visa's strong earnings outlook despite recent antitrust lawsuits, and Mastercard's strategic acquisition of Recorded Future for enhanced cybersecurity and value-added services.

title: Cantaloupe, Inc. Launches AdVantage Program
summary: Cantaloupe, Inc. (Nasdaq: CTLP) has launched its AdVantage program, enabling brands to engage consumers through digital advertising on its point-of-sale touchscreen devices across the U.S. and Canada. The program's first campaign is a collaboration with Mastercard (NYSE: MA) to support the Priceless Planet Coalition's reforestation efforts, encouraging donations with a matching commitment from Cantaloupe up to $500,000 and sweepstakes prizes. This initiative aims to drive sustainability and create new revenue opportunities for brands and operators while providing engaging consumer experiences.

title: VanEck establishes $30 million venture fund to support crypto and AI startups
summary: VanEck has launched a new $30 million venture fund, VanEck Ventures, to invest in early-stage companies in fintech, digital assets, and AI sectors. Led by Wyatt Lonergan and Juan Lopez, the fund targets investments between $500,000 and $1 million for 25-30 projects, with a focus on tokenization, internet-native financial marketplaces, and next-generation payment systems, particularly stablecoin innovations. This initiative aligns with VanEck's strategy to expand its involvement in the digital asset space beyond its existing ETF offerings.

title: Nuevo: BBDO Chile, Banco de Chile y Teletón buscan inspirar a las nuevas generaciones a donar
summary: BBDO Chile, Banco de Chile, and Teletón launched an animated campaign titled "Solidaridad: el orgullo de Chile" to encourage donations and inspire younger generations. The campaign highlights the beauty of Chile's landscapes and the pride the country feels for its people's solidarity during the Teletón. Produced by Believe, the initiative aims to boost participation in the charitable cause.

title: Citigroup Q3 Earnings: Profit Falls 9%, Investment Banking Revenue Soars, Mastercard and Apollo Partnerships
summary: Citigroup reported Q3 fiscal 2024 revenues which grew 1% year-over-year to $20.32 billion, beating analyst estimates, while GAAP EPS also surpassed expectations. Despite an investment banking revenue surge, net income fell 9% to $3.24 billion. The banking giant also highlighted new partnerships with Mastercard for cross-border payments and Apollo Global Management for a $25 billion private credit initiative.

title: NY Attorney General launches probe into Capital One’s $35.3bn deal with Discover Financial
summary: New York Attorney General Letitia James has launched an antitrust investigation into Capital One Financial's proposed $35.3bn acquisition of Discover Financial Services. The probe aims to determine if the merger violates state antitrust laws, given the significant credit card loan portfolios of both companies within New York and potential impacts on vulnerable consumers. Capital One has affirmed its pro-competitive stance and confidence in regulatory approval despite the investigation and customer lawsuits.

title: State of consumer digital payments in 2024
summary: Digital payment adoption continues to rise in the US and Europe, with a notable shift toward consumers initiating their shopping journeys with digital payments, not just using them at checkout. The article highlights the growth of in-app and in-store digital payments, the divergence of digital wallet preferences across regions and channels, and opportunities for ecosystem players to engage consumers earlier and innovate with rewards and account-to-account payments.

title: $1.07M Mastercard job posting class action settlement
summary: A $1.07 million Mastercard settlement has been reached to resolve claims that the company and its affiliates posted unlawful job listings in Washington state. The settlement benefits individuals who applied for a Mastercard job opening in Washington between Jan. 1, 2023, and July 19, 2024, where wage scale, salary range, or general benefits descriptions were not disclosed. Class members must submit a valid claim form by Nov. 4, 2024, to receive payments.

title: Insight Partners has paid out nearly $8 billion this year—but returns for its giant 2021 fund have mostly come up dry
summary: Insight Partners has returned nearly $8 billion to investors this year, a record high for the firm. However, most of these returns have not come from its $20 billion Fund XII, launched in 2021, which currently shows a negative net IRR. The fund's underperformance is attributed to the high valuations paid for companies during the 2021 tech bubble and the subsequent market "reset" in 2022, though experts suggest it is still too early to definitively judge the fund's long-term success.

title: Tap to Pay on iPhone expands to more European countries
summary: Apple has expanded its Tap to Pay on iPhone service to Austria, Czech Republic, Ireland, Romania, and Sweden, allowing millions of merchants to accept contactless payments securely using only an iPhone and a partner-enabled iOS app. This service supports payments from contactless credit/debit cards, Apple Pay, and other digital wallets without requiring additional hardware. Several payment platforms like Adyen, SumUp, and Viva.com are among the first to offer Tap to Pay on iPhone in these new countries, with more expected to follow.

title: Amtrak Offers 35,000 Bonus Points for New Amtrak Guest Rewards Preferred Cardholders
summary: Amtrak is offering a limited-time bonus of 35,000 points for new Amtrak Guest Rewards Preferred Mastercard holders who spend $2,000 within the first three billing cycles. These bonus points are valued at up to $930 in Amtrak travel, and cardholders can also earn accelerated points on travel and dining, along with benefits like companion coupons and lounge passes. The offer is valid from October 23 to December 4, 2024, aiming to incentivize holiday travelers to earn rewards for future trips across Amtrak's network.

title: Mastercard Earnings: Settling Into a Groove
summary: Mastercard's third-quarter earnings show increasing stability, mirroring Visa's performance but with slightly better margins. The company's long-term growth prospects and strong profitability are becoming clearer, with net revenue up 14% year over year and payment volume increasing by 10%. Morningstar maintains its fair value estimate of $465 per share, considering the stock to be fairly valued.

title: Is Visa a Debit Monopolist?
summary: The U.S. Justice Department has filed a lawsuit against Visa, alleging anti-competitive practices in the debit market. The DoJ claims Visa maintains dominance through exclusive contracts with card issuers that include incentives and punitive fees, thereby stifling competition and preventing rivals from gaining necessary scale. Visa, however, refutes these claims, stating that the debit market is dynamic and competitive, asserting it will vigorously defend itself against the "meritless" lawsuit.

title: Legal Fee Tracker: Lawsuit reveals fight over awards after $5.6 bln 'swipe fees' settlement
summary: A new lawsuit between class action law firms Scott + Scott and Robins Kaplan unveils a dispute over fees from the $5.6 billion "swipe fees" settlement involving Visa Inc and MasterCard Inc. Scott + Scott is suing Robins Kaplan for $5 million, alleging Robins Kaplan reneged on an agreement to ensure Scott + Scott received $20 million from the settlement's attorney fee awards. The case highlights the often-secretive nature of how class action law firms divide court-approved fee awards.

title: Fiserv exec opens up on Walmart, DoorDash partnerships
summary: Sunil Sachdev, Fiserv's head of embedded finance, discusses the company's recent high-profile partnerships with Walmart and DoorDash. The Walmart collaboration enables customers to pay directly from their bank accounts, while the DoorDash initiative provides drivers with faster payments and access to formal banking services. Sachdev emphasizes the growing importance of embedded finance and catering to non-traditional banking experiences, especially for gig economy workers.

title: Blackhawk Network Launches Digital Cards With Its Visa And Mastercard Branded e-Gift Products
summary: Blackhawk Network has launched new Visa and Mastercard branded e-gift cards that operate as digital-only products, leveraging QR code and tap-to-pay technology. These cards are designed to enhance security by encrypting card numbers and minimize fraud risk, building on consumer preference for digital payment methods. Consumers can scan a QR code at purchase to load funds directly to their mobile wallets for immediate online or in-store use.

title: Mastercard's 2030 Vision: A Future Without Passwords, Card Numbers
summary: Mastercard has announced its vision to transform online shopping by 2030, aiming to eliminate the need for physical card numbers, passwords, and one-time codes through tokenization and biometric authentication. This initiative seeks to streamline the checkout experience, enhance security, and is already underway in major markets with over 30% of Mastercard transactions globally currently tokenized. Despite this forward-looking announcement, Mastercard projects slower net revenue growth and lower EPS growth for 2025-2027 compared to previous forecasts.

title: Paying Attention to Investment Factors? You Should Be
summary: This article explores the concept of factor investing, noting that market leadership among factors like value, quality, and momentum is constantly changing. It details various investment factors, their historical performance, and why they might or might not continue to be successful, urging investors to consider them when building portfolios. The author questions whether quality and momentum, despite their recent strong performance, will continue to lead, and discusses the rationale behind sticking with underperforming factors like low volatility and size.

title: Riskified Launches Times Square Campaign to Combat $362B Ecommerce Fraud Crisis
summary: Riskified is participating in International Fraud Awareness Week from November 17-23, 2024, to highlight the severe threat of e-commerce fraud, which Juniper Research estimates will exceed $362 billion globally between 2023 and 2028. As part of its efforts, the company is launching a Times Square billboard campaign, powered by the New York Stock Exchange, to showcase "Safest Brands in Ecommerce" who prioritize fraud protection. This initiative, supported by various partners, aims to educate consumers and empower merchants with AI-powered fraud detection to create a safer holiday shopping season.

title: Logitech International S.A. (VTX:LOGN) is largely controlled by institutional shareholders who own 67% of the company
summary: Logitech International S.A. (VTX:LOGN) is primarily controlled by institutional shareholders, who collectively own 67% of the company, indicating the stock price is sensitive to their trading actions. BlackRock, Inc., Acadian Asset Management LLC, and The Vanguard Group, Inc. are among the largest institutional holders. Insiders own less than 1% but have been observed buying shares recently, while the general public holds a 33% stake.

title: The Mastercard Gamer Academy returns for 2025
summary: Mastercard has announced the return of its Gamer Academy for 2025, in partnership with G2 Esports and Riot Games. This development program aims to provide aspiring gaming professionals with resources, mentorship, and exclusive experiences, including trips to major League of Legends and VALORANT events. Participants will gain insights into various esports topics and receive networking opportunities, building on the success of the previous year's academy.

title: BNY to Manage U.S. Department of the Treasury's Largest Prepaid Debit Card Program for Federal Benefits - Direct Express
summary: BNY Mellon (BNY) has been selected by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service to manage the Direct Express® prepaid debit card program for federal benefits, serving approximately 3.4 million Americans. The five-year agreement begins on January 3, 2025, and will enhance cardholder experience with expanded customer service options, including online/digital funds access, bill pay, and cardless ATM access. Mastercard will continue as the payment network, with additional providers like Galileo Financial Technologies, MoCaFi, Senture, Sunrise Banks, and Ubiquity Global Services supporting the program.

title: Democrats bash CapOne-Discover merger proposal
summary: A group of Democratic lawmakers, including Sen. Elizabeth Warren and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, is urging federal regulators to closely scrutinize Capital One's proposed $35-billion acquisition of Discover Financial Services. They cite Capital One's history of regulatory infractions, including broken promises on community investment and penalties for consumer product abuses and anti-money laundering failures, as reasons for concern. Despite the opposition, financial services experts suggest the merger is likely to be approved due to potential benefits in credit card network competition.

title: 2024 Black Friday and Cyber Monday: Best golf deals and sales updated live
summary: This article compiles a live-updated list of the best Black Friday and Cyber Monday golf deals and sales for 2024. It covers discounts on various golf products, including shoes, apparel, equipment, electronics, bags, and accessories, from numerous retailers and brands. The author also includes exclusive promo codes for GNN readers to save on their purchases.

title: Mastercard reaches 'agreement in principle' to settle mass UK fees case
summary: Mastercard has reached an agreement in principle to settle a significant London lawsuit over card fees, brought on behalf of approximately 46 million British consumers. The settlement, which is subject to tribunal approval, aims to resolve a nearly decade-long legal battle following the UK's first mass consumer action of its kind. While claimants' lawyers had valued the entire claim at around 10 billion pounds, a person familiar with the agreement indicated a settlement figure of approximately 200 million pounds.

title: Global Payments spots 6 trends for next year
summary: Global Payments predicts six key trends for 2025, including enhanced fraud-fighting tools, embedded payments, and comprehensive point-of-sale systems. Their report, based on a survey of 600 companies, highlights increased investment in embedded payments and digital wallets by small and mid-sized businesses, along with the growing use of AI in biometrics and tap-to-pay transactions. The article also discusses the adoption of unified commerce platforms and payment orchestration across various sectors.

title: Mastercard agrees settlement in landmark interchange fee collective action
summary: Mastercard has agreed to a settlement in a significant UK collective action regarding alleged overcharging of credit card fees, a case that was once valued at £17bn. The deal, which needs approval from the Competition Appeal Tribunal (CAT) and is reportedly around £200 million, is opposed by the litigation funder, Innsworth Advisors, who plans to challenge it. Class representative Walter Merricks believes the settlement will provide meaningful compensation to consumers, while Mastercard aims to put the long-running case behind it.

title: Mastercard to Settle UK Fee Overcharging Suit for £200 Million
summary: Mastercard Inc. has agreed in principle to pay approximately £200 million ($254 million) to settle a class action lawsuit in the UK related to fee overcharging. The lawsuit, initially valued at £10 billion, was brought by Walter Merricks on behalf of roughly 46 million consumers and received court approval in 2021. This settlement averts what would have been the largest claim of its kind.

title: Citi, JP Morgan, others complete tokenization settlement trials
summary: Ten institutions, including Citi and J.P. Morgan, have completed simulated trials of the Regulated Settlement Network (RSN). These trials explored the use of a shared DLT network for settling tokenized transactions, building on previous Regulated Liability Network trials. The latest tests included tokenized Treasuries and investment-grade bonds, enabling delivery versus payment for wholesale transactions and exploring interoperability with external DLT networks.

title: Visa and Mastercard customers can get cash from $197.5m surcharge settlement - qualifying depends on your ATM use
summary: Visa and Mastercard have agreed to a $197.5 million settlement for allegedly imposing unlawful ATM surcharges and excessive interchange swipe fees. Customers who paid ATM surcharges between October 1, 2007, and July 26, 2024, through member banks like JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, and Bank of America, are eligible to file a claim. The deadline to submit a claim is January 22, 2025, and payments will vary based on the number of valid claims received.

title: Investing in Cybersecurity: PANW vs CRWD vs FTNT for NASDAQ:PANW by NaranjCapital
summary: This article provides a comparative analysis of three leading cybersecurity stocks: Palo Alto Networks (PANW), CrowdStrike (CRWD), and Fortinet (FTNT), examining their strengths, weaknesses, and growth strategies within a rapidly expanding cybersecurity market. It reviews global market trends, company overviews, strategic initiatives, financial performance including revenue, profit, valuation ratios, cash flow, and debt analysis, and major shareholders. The conclusion identifies Fortinet as the leading candidate despite debt concerns due to strong financials, while noting Palo Alto Networks' appealing valuation and CrowdStrike's recent setbacks.

title: NYC ad agencies Omnicom, Interpublic to form $30bn marketing powerhouse
summary: Omnicom is set to acquire Interpublic Group in a stock-for-stock deal, creating the world's largest advertising agency with combined annual revenue of almost $26bn and a market worth of over $30bn. The merger aims to accelerate innovation, leverage new technologies like AI, and achieve annual cost savings of $750m. The deal, which could face regulatory scrutiny, positions the combined entity, Omnicom, to better compete with tech giants and adapt to the evolving advertising landscape.

title: Tax
summary: Johnson Winter Slattery offers in-depth Australian tax advice and dispute resolution services to domestic and international corporations, covering a full spectrum of tax law including cross-border M&A and related party transactions. Their tax disputes team assists clients across various industries with interactions with the ATO and state revenue authorities, focusing on areas like GAAR, transfer pricing, and double tax agreements. The firm has a strong track record, representing major multinational clients and consistently receiving recognition from Chambers & Partners and Legal 500.

title: How stablecoins will eat payments, and what happens next
summary: Stablecoins are poised to disrupt the global payments industry by offering significantly lower fees, increased competition among payment providers, and wider accessibility compared to traditional systems. This shift will initially benefit businesses most burdened by current payment options, such as those with low margins or high transaction costs. As adoption grows, driven by the potential for increased profitability and improved features like instant finality and programmability, stablecoins will transition from niche solutions to mainstream payment platforms.

title: Mastercard to buy back up to $12 billion shares
summary: Mastercard has announced a new share repurchase program of up to $12 billion for its Class A shares, effective upon the completion of its current $11 billion program. The company also increased its quarterly dividend to 76 cents per share from 66 cents. Mastercard still has approximately $3.9 billion remaining under its existing buyback program as of December 13.

title: Shareholders Should Be Pleased With PayPal Holdings, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:PYPL) Price
summary: PayPal Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ:PYPL) has a P/E ratio of 19.7x, which is close to the US market median of 18x. The company has shown strong earnings growth, with a 25% gain in the last year and EPS up 5.0% over three years. Analysts forecast an annual EPS climb of 12% for the next three years, matching the broader market's predicted growth, suggesting shareholders are content with the current share price due to a lack of surprising events.

title: Visa INC Stock Opportunity: Investing for the Future
summary: This article explores the investment opportunity in Visa Inc. stock, highlighting its role as a global digital payments leader and its strong business model driven by transaction volumes. It details Visa's history, financial performance in 2022, key factors influencing its stock price, and profiles its largest individual and institutional shareholders. The piece concludes by outlining how to invest in Visa stock and provides tips for new investors.

title: Explore the Valuation Gaps in the S&P 500
summary: This article discusses the potential for value strategies in the S&P 500 for 2025, highlighting the current valuation gaps. William Nygren of Harris | Oakmark suggests that despite mega-cap tech driving market highs, other industries offer unusual opportunities for diversified portfolios of low P/E stocks. The Oakmark U.S. Large Cap ETF (OAKM) is presented as an actively managed fund targeting these value opportunities with a long-term horizon.

title: Global Payments Restructures with Strategic Cuts, Acquisitions, and Divestitures
summary: Global Payments is undergoing significant restructuring, involving job cuts, strategic acquisitions like Yazara, and potential divestitures of underperforming assets. This aims to boost efficiency, profitability, and market competitiveness, focusing on modernizing cloud solutions with Amazon and expanding its mobile POS offerings. The restructuring intends to streamline operations and strengthen Global Payments' market position in the evolving payments landscape.

title: 5 Things to Know About the Banc of California Los Angeles Football Club Mastercard
summary: This article reviews the Banc of California Los Angeles Football Club Mastercard, highlighting its features for LAFC superfans. It details the card's 1.5 points per dollar earned on all purchases, exclusive perks like free beer at home games and discounts on merchandise, and a sign-up bonus. The card previously offered a 0% introductory APR, but the article notes that the card is no longer available as the Banc of California stepped away from its naming rights deal with the LAFC stadium.

title: Latin America's $160 Billion E-Commerce Market Gets a Security Boost with Equifax and Mastercard Alliance
summary: Equifax and Mastercard have partnered to enhance security in Latin America's e-commerce market, which is projected to reach $160 billion by 2025. This alliance provides Mastercard business customers with advanced fraud management tools, including identity verification and chargeback prevention, through Equifax's Kount Payment Fraud solution. The goal is to reduce payment fraud and chargebacks, thereby improving the bottom line for businesses in the region.

title: Expedia Group, Wells Fargo, and Mastercard announce new suite of One Key credit cards
summary: Expedia Group, Wells Fargo, and Mastercard have announced a new suite of One Key credit cards. This collaboration will likely introduce new financial products aimed at consumers, potentially offering travel-related rewards and benefits through the One Key loyalty program.

title: How to Build a Product Customers Love and Drive Nearly $1B in Revenue Along the Way with Klaviyo CEO Andrew Bialecki
summary: Klaviyo CEO Andrew Bialecki shares insights on building a product customers love, scaling to nearly $1B in revenue, and their successful IPO in 2023. The article highlights Klaviyo's focus on solving problems for SMBs, leveraging an ecosystem approach, and strategically sequencing expansion into international and upmarket segments. Key takeaways include building a durable business with positive free cash flow and the importance of early-stage problem-solving.

title: DOJ's Visa antitrust lawsuit alleges debit card company monopoly
summary: The Justice Department has filed an antitrust lawsuit against Visa, accusing the company of running a debit card monopoly that imposed billions of dollars in additional fees on American consumers and businesses. The lawsuit claims Visa stifles competition and charges excessive fees by controlling over 60% of U.S. debit transactions. Visa denies the allegations, stating its network offers security and value.

title: Management That Matters: 2024’s Best U.S. Companies Unveiled
summary: The 2024 Drucker Institute Company Rankings identify the 30 best-managed U.S. companies based on corporate effectiveness across five categories: customer satisfaction, financial strength, social responsibility, innovation, and employee engagement. Apple secured the top spot as the best-managed company with an effectiveness score of 92.1, surpassing Microsoft from its 2023 position. Nvidia and Microsoft followed, with Intel and MasterCard rounding out the top five, demonstrating the importance of innovation and financial strength for high effectiveness scores.

title: Court approves Mastercard settlement
summary: A court approved a settlement agreement in which Mastercard will pay $26 million to resolve a class-action lawsuit alleging discrimination against Black, Hispanic, and female employees. The settlement also mandates annual pay audits and the hiring of a psychologist to evaluate the company's career ecosystem for bias. Mastercard disputed the allegations but agreed to the settlement to resolve the matter.

title: Mastercard agrees to $26 mln settlement in pay bias lawsuit
summary: Mastercard has agreed to a $26 million settlement and will audit its employment practices to resolve claims that it systematically underpaid approximately 7,500 female, Black, and Hispanic employees. Four former employees accused the company of routinely placing women and people of color in lower-paying roles, leading to smaller raises and fewer promotions compared to white men. Mastercard denies wrongdoing but stated the settlement is in the best interest of all involved.
